definition_zh: 准确的；精确的；精密的；忠实于事实的
definition_en: correct in every detail, exact in measurement, or faithful to the facts
core_image: 尺子贴紧木料边缘，刻度与墨线严丝合缝
scene: 木工把尺子压在板材上，反复核对后才下锯。The carpenter made an accurate cut along the pencil line.
sceneCN: 这里 accurate 指下刀的位置与画线完全吻合（第 7 个义项：做工精细准确）；句意为木匠沿着铅笔线切了一刀，位置分毫不差。

pos.zh: 形容词：准确的；精确的；精密的；忠实于事实的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「准确；精确度」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「准确地；精确地」
由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成，义为「不准确的；有错误的」
由 inaccurate 加后缀 -acy 构成，义为「不准确；错误之处」

senses.title: Correct and free from mistakes
senses.definition: containing no mistakes, especially of information, figures or details
senses.definitionCN: 尤指信息、数字或细节中没有错误
senses.example: Please check that the phone number on the form is accurate.
senses.exampleCN: 请核对一下表格上的电话号码是否准确。
senses.why: Latin cura is care: the word first means 'done with care', and careful checking is exactly what keeps a record free of mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cura 是「用心」：这个词最早是「用心做成」的意思，而核对时的用心正是让记录不出错的原因，于是「用心」就转成了「无误」。

senses.title: Exact in measurement
senses.definition: of an instrument, measurement or figure, able to give or show a true value within very small limits
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器、测量或数字能在很小的误差内给出或显示真实值
senses.example: A lab balance is far more accurate than a kitchen scale.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室天平比厨房秤精确得多。
senses.why: Care aimed at measuring means watching the smallest units; precision is care made visible on a scale.
senses.whyCN: 把「用心」用在测量上，就是盯住最小的单位；精密是「用心」在刻度上变得看得见的样子。

senses.title: True to the facts
senses.definition: of a description, report or memory, matching what actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 指描述、报道或记忆与实际发生的情况相符
senses.example: Her account of the accident was accurate in every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那场事故的叙述在每个细节上都准确。
senses.why: A report is a reckoning of events, and accurate marks whether that reckoning matches the events themselves.
senses.whyCN: 报道是对事件的一次核算，accurate 标记的正是这次核算与事件本身是否对得上。

senses.title: Faithful to an original
senses.definition: of a copy, translation or model, keeping the features of the original without adding or losing anything
senses.definitionCN: 指复制品、译本或模型保留原件的特征，不增不减
senses.example: The museum sells accurate replicas of the bronze mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆出售这面铜镜的精确复制品。
senses.why: Care can be turned towards an original: to reproduce it accurately is to follow it closely instead of inventing.
senses.whyCN: 「用心」也可以对着原件：准确地复制就是紧紧跟随原件，而不是自己另造。

senses.title: Well aimed or well judged
senses.definition: of a throw, shot or guess, landing exactly where it was meant to
senses.definitionCN: 指投掷、射击或猜测恰好落在预定的位置
senses.example: His pass was so accurate that the striker barely had to move.
senses.exampleCN: 他的传球极其精准，前锋几乎不用移动。
senses.why: The hand that is careful about aim is the same hand that is careful about numbers; both arrive at the intended point.
senses.whyCN: 对瞄准用心的手，与对数字用心的手是同一只手；两者都落在预定的那一点上。

senses.title: Correct in judgement
senses.definition: of a diagnosis, assessment or opinion, matching the true state of things
senses.definitionCN: 指诊断、评估或看法与真实情况相符
senses.example: The doctor's first diagnosis turned out to be accurate.
senses.exampleCN: 医生最初的诊断结果是准确的。
senses.why: Judgement is a reckoning of a situation; accuracy tests whether that reckoning holds.
senses.whyCN: 判断是对处境的一次核算；准确与否，就是检验这次核算站不站得住。

senses.title: Done with exact care
senses.definition: of work or a movement, carried out with close attention so that it fits the plan exactly
senses.definitionCN: 指活儿或动作在密切留意下完成，与预定的样子完全吻合
senses.example: The carpenter made an accurate cut along the pencil line.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠沿着铅笔线切了一刀，位置分毫不差。
senses.why: This is the word at its most physical: care shows in the fit between the tool and the line.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最具体的一面：「用心」体现在工具与那条线之间的严丝合缝上。

senses.title: Accurate to a stated limit
senses.definition: in the pattern accurate to, correct within a stated amount or decimal place
senses.definitionCN: 用于 accurate to 这一结构，表示误差不超过所说的量或小数位
senses.example: The thermometer is accurate to within half a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这支温度计的误差在半度以内。
senses.why: Care has a reach that can be named; the phrase states how small the permitted error is.
senses.whyCN: 「用心」有一个可以被说出来的限度；这个结构说的就是允许误差小到什么程度。

intro.en: Accurate is a Latin past participle built on cura 'care'; its history is the shift from 'done carefully' to 'free from error'.
intro.cn: accurate 是建立在 cura「用心」之上的拉丁语过去分词；它的历史就是从「用心做成」走向「没有差错」。

items.en: Cura meant 'care, concern, attention', and it also lies behind cure and curious.
items.cn: cura 意为「关心、留意、用心」，cure 与 curious 也出自它。

items.en: Curare 'to take care of, attend to' is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: curare 意为「照管、用心对待」，是这一整个词族的动词来源。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus curare formed accurare, 'to do with care, prepare carefully'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 curare 构成 accurare，意为「用心去做、仔细准备」。

items.en: The past participle accuratus meant 'prepared with care, exact', and English took the adjective whole.
items.cn: 过去分词 accuratus 意为「精心准备的、精确的」，英语把整个形容词借了过来。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English from the early seventeenth century, first for careful work and soon for exact figures and instruments.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十七世纪初进入英语，先指用心的活儿，很快又用于精确的数字与仪器。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family of forms; the near-meaning group gathers close synonyms that stress closeness to truth or to a standard.
note.cn: 形近组就是这个词自己的词族形式；近义组收强调贴近真相或贴近标准的近义词。

entries.definition: The quality of being correct or exact.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准确；精确度」，由本词加后缀 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that is correct and exact.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「准确地；精确地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不准确的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不准确；错误之处」，由 inaccurate 加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Marked by exactness in detail, often about measurement or wording.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精确的、确切的」，多指测量或措辞上的细致精确。

entries.definition: Completely correct in every detail, with no allowance left over.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精确的、丝毫不差的」，强调不留余量。

entries.definition: Right according to the facts or to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正确的」，强调符合事实或规则。

entries.definition: Showing great attention to small details in doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一丝不苟的」，强调做事时对细节极为留意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root cura 'care' and the everyday phrases the adjective appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 cura「用心」，以及这个词日常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Cura is care, so accurate work is literally work done with care.
normal.cn: cura 是「用心」，所以 accurate 的活儿字面上就是用心做出来的活儿。

normal.en: The same root gives cure: care is what both words are about.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 cure，两个词说的都是「用心照料」。

normal.en: Accurate figures are the ones you can check twice without finding a mistake.
normal.cn: accurate 的数字，就是你核对两遍也找不出错的那种。

normal.en: An accurate copy follows the original closely instead of adding anything.
normal.cn: accurate 的复制品紧贴原件，而不是自己添东西。

normal.en: Accurate to within half a degree tells you exactly how small the error may be.
normal.cn: 「accurate to within half a degree」把允许的误差说得明明白白。

abstract.cn: 想象尺子压在木板上，刻度与刀口之间没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Care is invisible; accuracy is what makes it visible on paper and on a dial.
abstract.cn: 用心是看不见的；准确就是让它在纸上和刻度盘上显形。

abstract.en: Things that are accurate can be checked by someone else, which is why the word suits facts and figures.
abstract.cn: 准确的东西别人也能核验，所以这个词特别适合事实与数字。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of accurate is care applied to some object: information, an instrument, a report, a copy, an aim, a diagnosis, a piece of work, or a stated margin of error.
sensesIntro.cn: accurate 的每个义项都是把「用心」用在某个对象上：信息、仪器、报道、复制品、瞄准、诊断、手上的活儿，或说出来的误差范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler pressed against the edge of a board, the mark and the blade meeting exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：尺子紧贴木板边缘，刻度与刀口正好对齐。

branches.en: FACTS AND REPORTS: care keeps information and descriptions matching what is true.
branches.cn: 事实与报道线：用心让信息与描述同真相保持一致。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: care becomes precision on an instrument, and the phrase accurate to names the margin of error.
branches.cn: 测量线：用心变成仪器上的精度，而 accurate to 结构把误差范围说出来。

branches.en: COPIES: care turned towards an original makes a faithful replica or translation.
branches.cn: 复制线：把用心对着原件，就得到忠实的复制品或译本。

branches.en: AIM AND JUDGEMENT: the hand and the mind both try to land on the right point.
branches.cn: 瞄准与判断线：手和心都试图落在正确的那一点上。

branches.en: WORKMANSHIP: the old physical sense, where care shows in how the tool meets the line.
branches.cn: 手艺线：最古老的具体的义，用心体现在工具与线如何相接。

definition_zh: 指责；控告；归咎；指控
definition_en: to say that someone has done something wrong, or to charge them formally with a crime
core_image: 一根手指直直指向对面的人，屋里所有人的目光都跟着转过去
scene: 会议室里有人把文件摔在桌上，声音一下子冷了下来。She accused him of hiding the report.
sceneCN: 这里 accuse 指当面指出对方做了错事（第 1 个义项：指责）；句意为她指责他把报告藏了起来。

pos.zh: 动词：指责；控告；归咎；指控

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「指控；指责」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「指控者；原告」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ory 构成，义为「指责的；控诉的」
由现在分词 accusing 加 -ly 构成，义为「带着责备地」

senses.title: To say someone did wrong
senses.definition: to say to someone's face that they have done something wrong, unfair or unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 当着某人的面说他做了错事、不公道的事或不可接受的事
senses.example: She accused him of hiding the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她指责他把报告藏了起来。
senses.why: Latin causa is a legal case, and accusare began as 'to bring a case against'; everyday blame is that courtroom gesture carried into ordinary rooms.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa 指「诉讼案件」，accusare 原本是「对某人提起诉讼」；日常的指责就是把法庭上那个手势搬进了普通房间。

senses.title: To charge with a crime
senses.definition: to state formally in court or in a police statement that someone has committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭或警方陈述中正式指出某人犯了罪
senses.example: The company was accused of tax fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被控税务欺诈。
senses.why: The courtroom is the oldest home of the word: to accuse is to state a charge that a court must answer.
senses.whyCN: 法庭是这个词最古老的家：accuse 就是提出一项需要法庭回应的指控。

senses.title: To blame a thing as the cause
senses.definition: to name a factory, policy, habit or other impersonal thing as the cause of harm
senses.definitionCN: 把损害的原因归到工厂、政策、习惯等非人的事物头上
senses.example: Many accuse social media of making young people anxious.
senses.exampleCN: 许多人把年轻人的焦虑归咎于社交媒体。
senses.why: If a case can be brought against a person, it can also be brought against anything that causes harm.
senses.whyCN: 既然可以对一个人提起诉讼，也就可以对任何造成损害的事物提起诉讼，于是它长出了「归咎于事物」的用法。

senses.title: To blame oneself
senses.definition: to say that you yourself have done something wrong, in the pattern accuse oneself
senses.definitionCN: 用 accuse oneself 的结构表示认定自己做错了事
senses.example: She accused herself of not calling sooner.
senses.exampleCN: 她责怪自己没有早点打电话。
senses.why: The accusing finger can turn back towards the speaker; the same charge is then laid on oneself.
senses.whyCN: 指责的手指也可以转回来指向说话者自己，同一项指控就落在了自己身上。

senses.title: The person charged in court
senses.definition: in the phrase the accused, the person or people charged with a crime in a court case
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the accused 这一说法，指刑事案件中被控犯罪的人
senses.example: The accused sat quietly beside her lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 被告安静地坐在她的律师身旁。
senses.why: A charge needs someone standing in the dock, and the passive participle became the name for that person.
senses.whyCN: 指控需要一个站在被告席上的人，被动分词就变成了那个人的称呼。

senses.title: A blaming look or tone
senses.definition: of a look, tone or gesture, showing that you think someone has done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 指目光、语气或动作表示出认定对方做错了事
senses.example: He gave me an accusing look across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他隔着桌子责备地看了我一眼。
senses.why: A pointing finger is a visible charge, so the participle also describes a look or tone that points without words.
senses.whyCN: 指着人的手指本身就是看得见的指控，于是分词也用来形容不用说话就在指人的目光或语气。

senses.title: To allege in an official report
senses.definition: to state publicly in a report, an investigation or the media that a person or group has done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 在报告、调查或媒体上公开指出某人或某群体做了错事
senses.example: The report accuses two officials of taking bribes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告指控两名官员收受贿赂。
senses.why: A case can be opened in public as well as in private; a report performs the same act before a wider court.
senses.whyCN: 案件既可以在私下提出，也可以在公众面前提出；一份报告就是在更大的法庭上做同一件事。

senses.title: To be wrongly blamed
senses.definition: of an innocent person, to be blamed for something they did not do, often in the phrase wrongly accused
senses.definitionCN: 指无辜的人被扣上并非自己所为的事，常见于 wrongly accused 这一说法
senses.example: He was wrongly accused and spent two years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 他被冤枉入狱两年。
senses.why: Because a charge can be false, the passive form carries the shadow of injustice: being accused is not the same as being guilty.
senses.whyCN: 指控可能是假的，所以被动形式也带着不公的阴影：被指控并不等于有罪。

intro.en: Accuse comes from Latin accusare 'to bring a charge', built on causa, the word for a legal case; the courtroom sense came first and the everyday one followed.
intro.cn: accuse 来自拉丁语 accusare「提出指控」，建立在表示「诉讼案件」的 causa 之上；法庭义在先，日常责怪义随后。

items.en: Causa meant 'cause, reason, motive' and also 'a legal case'; the legal sense is the one that shaped accuse.
items.cn: causa 意为「原因、理由、动机」，也指「诉讼案件」；塑造 accuse 的正是法律那一层意思。

items.en: Causari 'to plead, dispute, give as a reason' is a verb formed on causa.
items.cn: causari 意为「申辩、争讼、提出理由」，是由 causa 构成的动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to, against' plus causari gave accusare, 'to call to account, bring a charge against'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向、对着」加 causari 构成 accusare，意为「要求对账、提出指控」。

items.en: Old French acuser, recorded in the twelfth century, carried both the legal charge and the everyday blame.
items.cn: 古法语 acuser 见于十二世纪，同时带着法律指控与日常责怪两层意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb around 1300; the legal and the personal senses have travelled together ever since.
items.cn: 英语约在 1300 年借入这个动词；法律义与针对个人的责怪义从此一直同行。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family plus one Latin relative with a different prefix; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of blaming and formal charging.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词自己的词族，加上一个换了前缀的拉丁亲属词；近义组收表示责怪与正式指控的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root causa and the fixed patterns accuse actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 causa，以及 accuse 实际使用的固定结构。

normal.en: Causa is a case: to accuse is to bring a case against someone.
normal.cn: causa 是「案件」：accuse 就是对人提起一桩案子。

normal.en: The prefix ad- points forward, and so does the finger.
normal.cn: 前缀 ad- 朝前指，那根指责的手指也朝前指。

normal.en: The pattern is accuse someone of something, never accuse someone for something.
normal.cn: 固定结构是 accuse somebody of something，而不是用 for。

normal.en: The accused is the person standing in the dock, not the person speaking.
normal.cn: the accused 指站在被告席上的那个人，不是说话的人。

normal.en: An accusing look does the same work as a spoken charge, only without words.
normal.cn: 责备的目光做的是同一件事，只是没有说出口。

abstract.en: Picture one finger held out across a table while every other head turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指隔着桌子伸出去，其余的头都转了过来。

abstract.en: A charge is a line drawn around a person; the word is about where that line is placed.
abstract.cn: 指控就是在一个人周围画一条线；这个词关心的就是这条线画在哪里。

abstract.en: Because the line can be drawn wrongly, the word always carries the risk of injustice.
abstract.cn: 因为这条线可能画错，这个词永远带着不公的风险。

examples.en: She accused him of hiding the report.
examples.cn: 她指责他把报告藏了起来。

examples.en: Many accuse social media of making young people anxious.
examples.cn: 许多人把年轻人的焦虑归咎于社交媒体。

examples.en: He was wrongly accused and spent two years in prison.
examples.cn: 他被冤枉入狱两年。

sensesIntro.en: One gesture runs through all eight senses: a finger is pointed and a charge is laid, whether in a kitchen, a court, a public report, or back at the speaker.

branches.en: THE POINTED CHARGE: blame aimed at a person face to face, or at a thing that causes harm.
branches.cn: 当面指责线：把责任当面指向一个人，或指向造成损害的事物。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CHARGE: the court and the public report both state an allegation that must be answered.
branches.cn: 正式指控线：法庭与公开报告都在提出一项需要回应的指控。

branches.en: THE TURNED FINGER: the same charge can be laid on the speaker.
branches.cn: 回指线：同一项指控也可以落在说话者自己身上。

branches.en: THE DOCK: the passive participle names the person the charge is aimed at.
branches.cn: 被告席线：被动分词用来称呼被指控的那个人。

branches.en: THE UNSpoken CHARGE: a look can accuse without words, and a false charge leaves the mark of injustice.
branches.cn: 无声与冤屈线：目光不用说话也能指责，而错误的指控会留下不公的痕迹。

definition_zh: 实现；达到；完成；取得
definition_en: to succeed in reaching a goal, completing a task, or producing a result through effort
core_image: 爬到最后一级台阶，手终于碰到顶端的横杆
scene: 她练了整整一年，查分那天手指在屏幕上停了很久。She finally achieved the score she needed for the scholarship.
sceneCN: 这里 achieve 指够到某个分数标准（第 3 个义项：达到水平或标准）；句意为她终于达到了奖学金所需的分数。

senses.title: To reach a goal
senses.definition: to succeed in getting the result you planned and worked for
senses.definitionCN: 成功得到自己计划并为之努力的结果
senses.example: The team achieved its goal of cutting waste by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队实现了把浪费减少一半的目标。
senses.why: Old French achever is 'to come to a head': a goal is the head of an effort, and reaching it is achieving.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 achever 是「做到头」：目标是努力的那个「头」，碰到它就是 achieve。

senses.title: To complete a task
senses.definition: to finish or carry out a piece of work successfully, especially one that is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 成功做完或落实一件工作，尤指有难度的工作
senses.example: We achieved more in one morning than in the whole previous week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们一个上午做成的事比前整整一周还多。
senses.why: A task also has an end, and the verb first meant simply to bring work to that end.
senses.whyCN: 一件活儿也有它的尽头，这个动词最早的意思就是把工作带到那个尽头。

senses.title: To reach a level or standard
senses.definition: to reach a particular level, mark or standard, especially in study or sport
senses.definitionCN: 达到某个水平、分数或标准，尤用于学业或运动
senses.example: She finally achieved the score she needed for the scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 她终于达到了奖学金所需的分数。
senses.why: A standard is a line drawn at a certain height; to reach that line is the same 'coming to the top' applied to marks.
senses.whyCN: 标准是画在某一高度上的一条线；够到这条线，就是「到达顶端」用在分数上。

senses.title: To gain success or recognition
senses.definition: to gain something desirable such as success, respect or fame through effort
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力获得成功、尊重或名声等想要的东西
senses.example: He achieved fame only after his third novel.
senses.exampleCN: 他直到第三部小说之后才获得名声。
senses.why: What you gain by reaching the top can be named: success, fame and respect are the things waiting at the head of the climb.
senses.whyCN: 到达顶端所得到的东西可以被命名：成功、名声与尊重，就是等在攀登尽头的东西。

senses.title: To fulfil one's potential
senses.definition: to develop and use your abilities as fully as possible, in the pattern achieve your potential
senses.definitionCN: 尽可能充分地发展与运用自己的能力，见于 achieve your potential 这一说法
senses.example: Small classes help children achieve their potential.
senses.exampleCN: 小班教学帮助孩子发挥自己的潜能。
senses.why: If ability is a height a person could reach, fulfilling potential is coming to your own head, not someone else's.
senses.whyCN: 如果能力是一个人能够达到的高度，那么发挥潜能就是到达自己的那个顶端，而不是别人的。

senses.title: To produce an intended effect
senses.definition: to bring about a result or effect that was intended, especially in medicine, design or policy
senses.definitionCN: 产生原本想要的结果或效果，尤用于医药、设计或政策
senses.example: The new lighting achieves a warmer effect in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 新的灯光让屋里产生了一种更温暖的效果。
senses.why: Effort aimed at a design or a policy also has an intended end, and achieving the effect is reaching that end.
senses.whyCN: 投向设计或政策的努力也有一个预定的终点，做出预期效果就是到达那个终点。

senses.title: To bring about peace or agreement
senses.definition: to bring a settlement, agreement or reform into existence after effort and negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力与谈判使解决方案、协议或改革得以出现
senses.example: The two sides achieved a ceasefire after weeks of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数周谈判，双方促成了停火。
senses.why: An agreement is an end that two sides reach together, so the same verb covers treaties and ceasefires.
senses.whyCN: 协议是双方一起到达的终点，于是同一个动词也覆盖条约与停火。

senses.title: Performing at a level, in compounds
senses.definition: used in compounds such as high-achieving or low-achieving, describing how well a person or group performs
senses.definitionCN: 用于 high-achieving、low-achieving 等复合词，说明个人或群体的表现水平
senses.example: The school is known for its high-achieving students.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以学生成绩优异而闻名。
senses.why: The old image survives in compounds: a high-achieving student is one who has come to a high head in performance.
senses.whyCN: 古老的意象留在复合词里：high-achieving 的学生就是在表现上到达了较高顶端的人。

intro.en: Achieve comes from a French verb meaning 'to bring to a head', built on Latin caput 'head'; the idea of reaching the top has never left it.
intro.cn: achieve 来自一个意为「带到顶端」的法语动词，建立在拉丁语 caput「头」之上；「到达顶端」这个意象从未离开过它。

items.en: Caput meant 'head', and the phrase ad caput 'to the head' expressed reaching a top or an end.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」，短语 ad caput「到头」表示到达顶端或终点。

items.en: A spoken Latin phrase *ad caput is reconstructed as the source of the French verb; the exact form is reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为通俗拉丁语短语 *ad caput 是这个法语动词的来源；确切形式属于重构，并无文献记录。

items.en: Achever 'to finish, bring to an end' grew from venir a chief 'to come to a head', where chief comes from Latin caput.
items.cn: achever「完成、带到终点」由短语 venir a chief「到达顶端」发展而来，其中 chief 来自拉丁语 caput。

items.en: English borrowed the verb around 1300 with the sense 'to finish, accomplish'; the modern spelling settled later.
items.cn: 英语约在 1300 年借入这个动词，义为「完成、做成」；现在的拼写是后来才定下来的。

items.en: The sense widened from finishing a piece of work to succeeding in reaching a goal, a standard or a result.
items.cn: 词义从「把活儿做完」扩展到「成功达到目标、标准或结果」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family of forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of reaching and completing, each with a slightly different emphasis.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词自己的词族形式；近义组收表示「到达」与「完成」的动词，各自侧重点略有不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French and Latin pieces behind the word, plus the phrases it usually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用这个词背后真实的法语与拉丁语构件，以及它常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Achever is to bring to a head, and caput is a head: achieve is to reach the top of a climb.
normal.cn: achever 是「做到头」，caput 是「头」：achieve 就是爬到攀登的顶端。

normal.en: Chief and achieve share the Latin head, which is why the word feels like arriving somewhere.
normal.cn: chief 与 achieve 共享拉丁语的「头」，所以这个词有一种「抵达某处」的感觉。

normal.en: You achieve a goal, a result or a standard, never an object you can hold.
normal.cn: 搭配是 achieve a goal、a result、a standard，而不是拿到一件能握在手里的东西。

normal.en: Achievement adds -ment, turning the act of reaching into a thing you can point at.
normal.cn: achievement 加 -ment，把「到达」的动作变成一件可以指着看的东西。

normal.en: High-achieving keeps the old picture: a student who has climbed to a high place.
normal.cn: high-achieving 保留着旧画面：一个已经爬到高处的学生。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on the top bar of a ladder, the last step still under the foot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抓住梯子顶端的横杆，最后一级台阶还在脚下。

abstract.en: Every sense has a top: a goal, a task, a mark, a fame, a potential, an effect, an agreement.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都有一个「顶」：目标、任务、分数、名声、潜能、效果、协议。

abstract.en: The word never means simply receiving something; the top must be climbed to.
abstract.cn: 这个词从来不只是「收到」什么；那个顶端必须爬上去才够得到。

examples.en: The team achieved its goal of cutting waste by half.
examples.cn: 这个团队实现了把浪费减少一半的目标。

examples.en: She finally achieved the score she needed for the scholarship.
examples.cn: 她终于达到了奖学金所需的分数。

examples.en: The two sides achieved a ceasefire after weeks of talks.

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of achieve ends at a top of some kind: a goal, a task, a mark, a reputation, one's own ability, an intended effect, an agreement, or a level of performance.
sensesIntro.cn: achieve 的每个义项都止于某种「顶」：目标、任务、分数、名声、自己的能力、预期的效果、协议，或某个表现水平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on the top bar of a ladder, the last step still under the foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手抓住梯子顶端的横杆，最后一级台阶还在脚下。

branches.en: GOAL AND TASK: an aim or a piece of work has an end, and reaching it is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 目标与任务线：一个目标或一件活儿都有尽头，到达它就是最基本的义项。

branches.en: MARK AND REWARD: a standard is a line to reach, and success or fame is what waits beyond it.
branches.cn: 分数与收获线：标准是一条要够到的线，成功与名声就是线那一边等着的东西。

branches.en: ONE'S OWN HEIGHT: potential is the top a person could reach, so fulfilling it is coming to your own head.
branches.cn: 自身高度线：潜能是一个人可能达到的顶端，发挥潜能就是到达自己的那个顶端。

branches.en: INTENDED ENDS: an effect or an agreement is an end that effort is aimed at and finally reaches.
branches.cn: 预定终点线：效果或协议是努力所朝向、并最终到达的终点。

branches.en: MEASURED PERFORMANCE: the old head image survives in compounds about how high a person has climbed.
branches.cn: 表现水平线：古老的「头」意象留在复合词里，说明一个人爬到了多高。

senses.title: Something done successfully through effort
senses.definition: a thing that has been done successfully, especially after hard work
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力成功做成的事情，尤指来之不易的成果
senses.example: Winning the scholarship was her biggest achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 拿到奖学金是她最大的成就。
senses.why: The Old French verb meant to bring something to a head, and the noun names the point where the work is finally finished.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词的意思是「把事情带到头」，名词所指的就是工夫下到头的那个点：事情做成了。

senses.title: The act of reaching a goal
senses.definition: the successful reaching of a goal or standard
senses.definitionCN: 成功达到某个目标或标准
senses.example: The achievement of full independence took many years.
senses.exampleCN: 实现完全独立花了许多年。
senses.why: A goal is a head or end point, and achieving is the movement that carries you to it.
senses.whyCN: 目标是那个「头」或终点，而达成就是把人一路带到那里的过程。

senses.title: A notable deed worth remembering
senses.definition: an impressive deed or feat, often one that is recorded or celebrated
senses.definitionCN: 令人称叹的作为或壮举，常被记载或传颂
senses.example: Landing on the moon was a remarkable achievement of the twentieth century.
senses.exampleCN: 登月是二十世纪一项非凡的壮举。
senses.why: Once a deed is finished, it can stand on its own as a landmark, so the word shifts from the doing to the thing done.
senses.whyCN: 一件作为一旦完成，就能独立地立成一块界碑；于是词义从「做」转向「做成的事」。

senses.title: Performance measured in study or work
senses.definition: the level of success a person reaches in school or at work, often measured by tests or results
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在学校或工作中达到的成功水平，常以测验或成果衡量
senses.example: The school tracks the achievement of every student in reading and maths.
senses.exampleCN: 学校跟踪每个学生在阅读和数学上的成绩。
senses.why: Institutions needed a countable measure of finished work, so the noun was applied to the results themselves.
senses.whyCN: 学校与机构需要一种可计量的「完成度」，于是这个词被用来指那些结果本身。

senses.title: A feeling of pride at having done well
senses.definition: the pride and satisfaction that come from doing something well, especially in the phrase a sense of achievement
senses.definitionCN: 把一件事做好之后产生的自豪与满足，尤用于搭配 a sense of achievement
senses.example: She felt a real sense of achievement after fixing the bike herself.
senses.exampleCN: 自己修好自行车后，她感到了真正的成就感。
senses.why: The finished deed leaves an inner echo, and the word names that echo as a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 做成的事会在人心里留下回声，这个词把这个回声命名为一种感受。

senses.title: An award for success
senses.definition: a prize or honour given to someone for what they have accomplished, as in achievement award
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的作为而授予的奖项或荣誉，如成就奖
senses.example: He received a lifetime achievement award at the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他在典礼上获得了终身成就奖。
senses.why: A society marks a finished feat with a token, and the token borrows the name of the feat.
senses.whyCN: 社会用一件信物来标记已完成的功业，信物便借用了功业的名字。

senses.title: A record of what one has done
senses.definition: the sum of a person's successes, looked at as evidence of ability
senses.definitionCN: 一个人成功之事的总体，被当作能力的凭证来看
senses.example: Her record of achievement made her the obvious choice for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她的业绩记录使她成为这个职位的当然人选。
senses.why: Several finished deeds pile up into a record, and the word moves from one item to the whole pile.
senses.whyCN: 若干件做成的事堆叠起来就成了记录，词义也就从单件移到了整堆。

senses.title: Used ironically for something hardly impressive
senses.definition: used ironically to describe something that is not impressive at all
senses.definitionCN: 反讽地用于形容根本不值得称道的事
senses.example: You forgot your own birthday? That is quite an achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 你连自己的生日都忘了？可真了不起。
senses.why: A word for hard-won success is turned upside down when the deed is trivially easy, and the irony works because the image stays so positive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指来之不易的成功；当事情轻易到近乎荒唐时，把它倒过来用，反讽正因为原意象太正面才成立。

intro.en: Achievement is a French noun built on a Latin word for the head, and the whole family still carries the image of a task brought to its end.
intro.cn: achievement 是一个建立在拉丁语「头」之上的法语名词，整个词族仍带着「把事情带到头」的意象。

items.en: Caput meant 'head'. It is the source of capital, captain and chief, and through chief it lies behind achievement.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」。它是 capital、captain 与 chief 的来源，而 achievement 经由 chief 上溯到此。

items.en: A phrase usually reconstructed as ad caput, 'to the head', is thought to have produced a verb meaning to bring something to its head or end.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构为 ad caput「到头」的短语，产生了表示「把某事带到头、带到终点」的动词。

items.en: Achever meant 'to finish, bring to an end', and also 'to win, acquire'; the h was added in French spelling.
items.cn: achever 意为「完成、结束」，也有「赢得、取得」之义；法语拼写中加进了 h。

items.en: The noun achevement meant 'a finishing, an end', and later 'a deed carried out'.
items.cn: 名词 achevement 意为「完成、了结」，后来指「做成的事」。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain, and the sense moved from completion to a notable deed.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个词；确切首见年代不确定，词义从「完成」转向「值得称道的作为」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the achieve family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for success and for what has been reached.
note.cn: 形近组是 achieve 一族；近义组列出表示成功与已达到之物的其他词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to succeed in doing or reaching something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现、取得、达到」。

entries.definition: Able to be done or reached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可实现的、可达到的」。

entries.definition: A person who succeeds, especially through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有成就的人」，尤指靠努力成功的人。

entries.definition: Someone who does better than expected, sometimes at a cost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成绩超出预期的人」，有时带代价意味。

entries.definition: Something done successfully; close to achievement but often used of a completed task.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就、完成的事」，与 achievement 相近，更强调任务已完成。

entries.definition: The reaching of a goal or standard; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「达到、造诣」，语气正式。

entries.definition: An impressive act that requires skill, strength or courage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「壮举、非凡的作为」，强调技巧、力量或勇气。

entries.definition: The fact of doing well or of something working out; broader than achievement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成功」，范围比 achievement 更宽，不限于具体做成的事。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French and Latin background and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的法语与拉丁语背景，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The root is chief, 'head': achieving is bringing a task to its head, its end.
normal.cn: 词根是 chief「头」：achieving 就是把事情带到头、带到终点。

normal.en: Achieve, achievable, achiever and achievement keep the same ending shape.
normal.cn: achieve、achievable、achiever、achievement 保留着同一套词尾形状。

normal.en: Schools say academic achievement when they mean measured results.
normal.cn: 学校说 academic achievement 时，指的是被量化的成绩。

normal.en: A sense of achievement is the good feeling that follows finished work.
normal.cn: a sense of achievement 是事情做完之后随之而来的好感觉。

normal.en: A lifetime achievement award honours a whole career, not one day.
normal.cn: a lifetime achievement award 表彰的是整个职业生涯，而不是某一天。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase: each step is effort, and the top landing is the achievement.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯：每一级都是努力，顶端那块平台就是成就。

abstract.en: The word can point at the deed, the record of deeds, or the glow left inside: one success seen from three distances.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以指那件事、那串记录，也可以指心里留下的光：同一份成功，从三种距离看。

abstract.en: Irony works because the picture stays bright while the deed grows small.
abstract.cn: 反讽之所以成立，是因为画面依旧明亮，而事情却小得可笑。

examples.en: Finishing the marathon was a huge achievement for a man of his age.
examples.cn: 跑完马拉松对他这个年纪的人来说是了不起的成就。

examples.en: The team celebrated the achievement of its first clean audit.
examples.cn: 团队庆祝首次通过无保留审计这一成果。

examples.en: She keeps a notebook listing every small achievement of the week.
examples.cn: 她有一本笔记，记下每周每一件小小的成就。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额吃夫门特」——一路吃劲推到终点，推开的门后就是成果：成就、达成。

root: 英语 achievement 来自古法语 achevement「完成」，更早是 achever「把事情做到头」，源于通俗拉丁语 ad caput「到头」，而 caput 是拉丁语「头」；同族还有 chief、capital、captain。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses come from one picture: work brought to its head. The differences are whether the word points at the deed, the arriving, the measured result, the feeling, the prize, the record, or an ironic reversal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自同一个画面：工夫下到了头。区别只在于词指向的是那件事、抵达的动作、被计量的结果、心里的感受、奖项、履历，还是一次反讽式的倒转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase whose top landing is finally reached.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段楼梯，顶端的平台终于被踩在脚下。

branches.en: THE DEED: the finished thing stands as a landmark of effort.
branches.cn: 事情线：做成的事作为努力的界碑立在那里。

branches.en: THE GOAL: the word names the act of arriving at the head or end point.
branches.cn: 目标线：这个词指的是抵达那个「头」或终点的动作。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: schools and employers count finished work as results and records.
branches.cn: 计量线：学校与雇主把完成的工作计为成绩与记录。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the finished deed echoes back as pride.
branches.cn: 感受线：做成的事以自豪的形式回声般返回。

branches.en: THE MARK: a prize honours the deed, while irony shrinks it to nothing.
branches.cn: 标记线：奖项为功业加冕，反讽则把它缩到极小。

intro.en: The word is a French noun built on a Latin head, and English keeps the whole family around achieve.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「头」之上的法语名词，英语则围绕 achieve 保留了整族词。

latinIntro.en: Only caput and ad are recorded Latin; the intermediate phrase is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 有文献记录的拉丁语只有 caput 与 ad，中间那个短语属于重构形式。

items.example: It points the action towards a goal.
items.exampleCN: 它把动作指向一个目标。

items.example: Caput is the source of capital and captain.
items.exampleCN: caput 是 capital 与 captain 的来源。

items.example: Chief carries the same head image into English.
items.exampleCN: chief 把同一个「头」的意象带进英语。

items.meaning: to finish, bring to an end
items.example: The verb joins the prefix and the head.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把前缀与「头」合在一起。

items.example: The noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 她达到了目标。
它把 achieve 变成 achievement。
它构成 achievable。
它构成 overachiever。

definition_zh: 酸；酸味；酸性；酸液；尖刻的
definition_en: a chemical substance that reacts with a base, a sour taste or quality, or a sharp and bitter manner
core_image: 柠檬汁滴在舌尖，整张脸立刻缩紧
scene: 她切开一只青柠，汁水溅到指尖，顺手吮了一下。The acid in the lemon made her wince.
sceneCN: 这里 acid 指柠檬里那种起反应的酸性物质（第 1 个义项：能与碱反应的化学物质）；句意为柠檬里的酸让她皱起了脸。

pos.zh: 名词：酸；酸味；酸性；酸液
形容词：酸性的；尖刻的

collocations.zh: 严峻的考验；决定性检验

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「酸性的；尖刻的」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「酸度；酸性」
由本词加 -ify 构成，义为「使变酸；酸化」
由 acidify 加 -ation 构成，义为「酸化过程」

senses.title: A chemical compound that reacts with a base
senses.definition: a substance that reacts with a base and turns litmus red, or a solution containing it
senses.definitionCN: 能与碱反应、使石蕊变红的物质，或含有这种物质的溶液
senses.example: Citric acid gives lemons their sharp taste.
senses.exampleCN: 柠檬酸使柠檬带上尖酸的滋味。
senses.why: Latin acidus simply meant sour; chemistry later fixed the word on the class of substances that taste sour and react with bases.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acidus 本只表示「酸的」；化学后来把这个词固定到那一类尝起来发酸、又能与碱反应的物质上，起点仍是「酸」这一味觉。

senses.title: The sharp taste of lemon or vinegar
senses.definition: the sharp sour taste of lemon, vinegar or unripe fruit
senses.definitionCN: 柠檬、醋或未熟水果那种尖锐的酸味
senses.example: The clean acid of the grapefruit cuts through the rich sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 西柚清爽的酸味化解了浓重的酱汁。
senses.why: This is the sense the Latin adjective named first: a taste on the tongue, before any chemistry existed.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语形容词最早命名的义项：化学尚未出现之前，它就是舌头上的一种味道。

senses.title: The property of being acidic
senses.definition: the state of a soil, water or solution having a pH below seven
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、水或溶液酸碱度低于七的状态
senses.example: Farmers add lime to reduce the acid in the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 农民施石灰来降低土壤的酸性。
senses.why: From the taste, the word was extended to the measurable property that produces the taste.
senses.whyCN: 人们从「尝到的酸」进一步指向「造成这种酸的可测性质」，于是有了酸性。

senses.title: A strong corrosive liquid
senses.definition: a strong acid in liquid form, especially one that can burn skin or metal
senses.definitionCN: 液态的强酸，尤指能灼伤皮肤或腐蚀金属的那种
senses.example: The battery acid had eaten a hole in the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 电池酸液把地面蚀出了一个洞。
senses.why: The substance at its strongest becomes something you can pour, spill and be burned by, so the word names a dangerous liquid rather than a class.
senses.whyCN: 当这种物质浓到极处，就成了能倒、能洒、能灼人的东西；词义于是从「类别」落到一瓶危险的液体上。

senses.title: Bitter and cutting in manner
senses.definition: of a remark, tone or humour, sharp and unkind
senses.definitionCN: 指言语、语气或幽默尖锐而不留情面
senses.example: He made an acid comment about her new haircut.
senses.exampleCN: 他对她的新发型说了一句尖刻的话。
senses.why: A sour taste in the mouth is the body's own picture of a sour temper, so the taste word becomes a manner word.
senses.whyCN: 嘴里的酸是身体对坏脾气的现成比喻，于是味觉词自然变成了形容态度的词。

senses.title: The acid test: a decisive check
senses.definition: in the phrase acid test, a test that proves whether something really works or is genuine
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 the acid test，指能证明某物是否真的有效或真实的检验
senses.example: The cold winter was the acid test for the new heating system.
senses.exampleCN: 这个寒冬是对新供暖系统的严峻考验。
senses.why: Nitric acid was once used to tell real gold from false, and the phrase keeps that image of a test that settles the question.
senses.whyCN: 硝酸曾被用来分辨真金与假金，这个短语保留了「一试便见分晓」的画面。

senses.title: Rain made acidic by pollution
senses.definition: in acid rain, rain made acidic by gases released from burning fuel
senses.definitionCN: 用于 acid rain，指因燃烧燃料释放的气体而变酸的雨
senses.example: Acid rain has damaged forests across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 酸雨已经损害了这一带的森林。
senses.why: The adjective carries the chemical property into the weather, so a laboratory word ends up in the sky.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把这个化学性质带进了天气里，实验室里的词于是升到了天上。

senses.title: A sour boiled sweet
senses.definition: in British English, an acid drop: a small hard sweet with a sharp sour flavour
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中 acid drop 指一种小而硬、味道尖酸的糖果
senses.example: Grandma always kept a bag of acid drops in her handbag.
senses.exampleCN: 外婆的手提包里总放着一袋酸味硬糖。
senses.why: The taste that named the word comes back as the name of the sweet, because that sharp flavour is the whole point of the thing.
senses.whyCN: 当初给这个词命名的味道，回头成了糖果的名字，因为那股尖酸正是这种糖存在的理由。

intro.en: Acid goes back to a Latin adjective for sour, and every branch of meaning still starts from a taste on the tongue.
intro.cn: acid 上溯到一个表示「酸的」的拉丁语形容词，所有义项都从舌头上的味道出发。

items.en: The root *h₂eḱ- is generally reconstructed as 'sharp, pointed'; it is the source of Latin acer 'sharp' and acus 'needle'. Its link with sourness is old, but the exact path is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语词根 *h₂eḱ- 表示「尖锐的」，是拉丁语 acer「尖锐的」与 acus「针」的来源；它与「酸」的联系很古老，但具体路径不确定。

items.en: The verb acere meant 'to be sour, be sharp', and the same family produced acetum 'vinegar'.
items.cn: 动词 acere 意为「发酸、带尖味」，同一词族还产生 acetum「醋」。

items.en: Acidus was the adjective for 'sour, tart, sharp', and it is the form English took.
items.cn: acidus 是表示「酸的、尖酸的」的形容词，英语借入的正是这个形式。

items.en: The neuter form acidum was used as a noun for a sour substance, and alchemists and early chemists applied it to acids as a class.
items.cn: 其中性形式 acidum 被当作名词，指带酸味的物质；炼金术士与早期化学家又用它指一整类酸。

items.en: English borrowed acid in the early seventeenth century as both adjective and noun; the chemical class sense settled soon after, and the figurative 'bitter' sense followed. Exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪初同时借入形容词与名词用法；化学类别义随后稳定下来，比喻的「尖刻」义再往后出现。确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acid family in English; the near-meaning group gathers words for sourness and for eating away.
note.cn: 形近组是英语里的 acid 词族；近义组列出表示酸味与腐蚀的相关词。

entries.definition: Containing acid or having a pH below seven.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸性的、含酸的」，指酸碱度低于七。

entries.definition: The amount of acid in a substance, or a sour quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸度、酸性」，也指尖酸的意味。

entries.definition: To make something acid or become acid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变酸、酸化」。

entries.definition: The process of becoming acid, especially in soil or seawater.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸化过程」，多用于土壤或海水。

entries.definition: Having the taste of lemon or vinegar; the everyday word for what acid names technically.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸的」，是 acid 在技术义之外的日常说法。

entries.definition: Sharp and sour in a pleasant way, often of fruit or a small pie.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸而爽口的」，多形容水果或小馅饼。

entries.definition: Able to burn or eat away material; also used of bitterly cutting remarks.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腐蚀性的」，也形容言语刻薄伤人。

entries.definition: Able to destroy metal or living tissue by chemical action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腐蚀性的」，指通过化学作用破坏金属或活体组织。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin words and the everyday phrases acid appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁词，以及 acid 常出现的日常搭配展开。

normal.en: Acidus is Latin for sour, and acere is the verb 'to be sour'.
normal.cn: acidus 是拉丁语「酸的」，acere 是动词「发酸」。

normal.en: The same family gives vinegar its Latin name acetum.
normal.cn: 同一词族给了醋一个拉丁名字 acetum。

normal.en: Acid rain, acid test and acid reflux each carry a different edge of the same word.
normal.cn: acid rain、acid test、acid reflux 各自带着这个词不同的一面。

normal.en: An acid remark leaves the same taste in the ear that lemon leaves in the mouth.
normal.cn: 一句 acid remark 在耳朵里留下的味道，和柠檬在嘴里留下的一样。

normal.en: An acid drop is a sweet that tastes of the word itself.
normal.cn: acid drop 是一颗尝起来就像这个词的糖。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of lemon juice: the whole word starts there, then spreads into chemistry, weather, speech and sweets.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴柠檬汁：整个词从这里开始，然后蔓延到化学、天气、言语和糖果。

abstract.en: Sourness is a warning on the tongue, which is why the word also serves for words that sting.
abstract.cn: 酸是舌头上的警报，所以这个词也用来形容刺人的话。

abstract.en: The strongest acid is the one you can spill, so the word slides from taste to danger.
abstract.cn: 最强的酸是能洒出来的那种，于是词义从味道滑向危险。

examples.en: The acid in the lemon made her wince.
examples.cn: 柠檬里的酸让她皱起了脸。

examples.en: This soil is too acid for most vegetables.
examples.cn: 这块土对多数蔬菜来说酸性太强。

examples.en: He answered with an acid tone that ended the conversation.
examples.cn: 他用一种尖刻的语气回答，谈话就此结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱吸的」——小孩爱吸酸的柠檬，吸一口脸就皱起来：酸、酸味。

root: 拉丁语 acidus「酸的」来自动词 acere「发酸、带尖味」，同一词族有 acetum「醋」；更早一般认为与表示「尖锐」的印欧词根 *h₂eḱ- 有关，具体路径不确定。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses begin with one bodily fact: something tastes sharp. Chemistry names the substance, cooking names the taste, farming names the property, industry names the liquid, and speech borrows the sting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于同一个身体事实：有东西尝起来是尖酸的。化学命名物质，烹饪命名味道，农事命名性质，工业命名液体，而言语借走了那股刺痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of lemon juice on the tongue, and the face pulling tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴柠檬汁落在舌尖，整张脸缩紧。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: chemistry turns the taste into a class of compounds and into a liquid strong enough to burn.
branches.cn: 物质线：化学把这种味道变成一类化合物，也变成能灼人的液体。

branches.en: THE TASTE AND ITS MEASURE: what the tongue feels becomes a property that can be tested in soil and water.
branches.cn: 味道与度量线：舌头感到的东西，变成了可在土壤和水中测量的性质。

branches.en: THE VOICE: a sour mouth becomes a sour temper, so the word describes cutting remarks.
branches.cn: 言语线：嘴里的酸变成脾气的酸，于是这个词用来形容刻薄的话。

branches.en: THE PROOF: acid once separated real gold from false, and the phrase still means a test that settles the matter.
branches.cn: 检验线：酸曾经用来分辨真假黄金，短语至今仍指一试便知分晓的检验。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY EDGE: the same word rides in the rain and sits in a bag of sour sweets.
branches.cn: 日常线：同一个词既藏在雨里，也躺在一袋酸糖里。

intro.en: Acid is a Latin adjective turned English noun and adjective, and its family is built with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: acid 是一个由拉丁语形容词转成的英语名词兼形容词，其词族用普通后缀扩展而来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verbs and nouns below are recorded; only the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语动词与名词均有文献记录，只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The root carries the taste into every derivative.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把那股味道带进每一个派生词。

items.example: It ends the Latin adjective acidus.
items.exampleCN: 它收束了拉丁语形容词 acidus。
它构成 acidic。
它构成 acidity。
它构成 acidify。

items.example: Acere is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: acere 是形容词背后的动词。

items.example: Acetum is the sour liquid itself.
items.exampleCN: acetum 就是那种酸味的液体。

items.example: Acidus is the direct source of acid.

它构成 amino acid。

definition_zh: 承认；认错；确认收到；致谢；认可
definition_en: to admit that something is true, to confirm that you have received something, or to show recognition and thanks
core_image: 收到信后回一句「我看到了」，让对面那个人放下悬着的心
scene: 他发出邮件后一直盯着手机，只等一句回话。Please acknowledge my email so I know you received it.
sceneCN: 这里 acknowledge 指「告知已收到」（第 3 个义项：确认收到某物）；句意为请回复确认你已收到我的邮件，好让我知道。

pos.zh: 动词：承认；认错；确认收到；致谢；认可

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「承认；致谢；收到通知」
同上的英式拼写，义为「承认；致谢；确认收到」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「公认的；得到承认的」
由 un- 加本词加 -ed 构成，义为「未被承认的；未获答复的」

senses.title: Admit that something is true
senses.definition: to accept or admit that a fact, situation or claim is true
senses.definitionCN: 接受或承认某个事实、情况或说法是真实的
senses.example: She acknowledged that the delay was her fault.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认延误是她的责任。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to know and then to recognize; acknowledging is saying out loud what you already know to be true.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「知道」，进一步引申为「认出」；承认就是把心里已经知道为真的东西说出来。

senses.title: Admit a fault or responsibility
senses.definition: to admit that you did something wrong or that you are responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 承认自己做错了事，或承认自己对此负有责任
senses.example: The company finally acknowledged its role in the pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 公司最终承认了自己在污染中所起的作用。
senses.why: Knowing a fault and naming it are two different steps; the word marks the second, harder step.
senses.whyCN: 知道自己有错，与把错说出口，是两步；这个词标出的是更难的那一步。

senses.title: Confirm that something has arrived
senses.definition: to tell someone that you have received a message, letter, order or payment
senses.definitionCN: 告诉对方已收到某封信、某条消息、某笔订单或款项
senses.example: Please acknowledge my email so I know you received it.
senses.exampleCN: 请回复确认你已收到我的邮件，好让我知道。
senses.why: A message only counts as delivered when the other side shows that it has registered it, so recognition becomes receipt.
senses.whyCN: 一条消息只有在对方表示「已登记」时才算真正送达，于是「认出」变成了「确认收到」。

senses.title: Thank someone for help
senses.definition: to publicly thank a person or group for their help or support
senses.definitionCN: 公开感谢某人或某个群体给予的帮助与支持
senses.example: The author acknowledged her students in the preface.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在序言里向学生们致谢。
senses.why: To recognize a kindness is also to admit a debt, so thanks and admission share one verb.
senses.whyCN: 承认别人的好意，也就等于承认自己欠了一份情；于是致谢与承认共用一个动词。

senses.title: Recognize a right or authority
senses.definition: to accept the existence or validity of someone's right, status or power
senses.definitionCN: 接受某人的权利、地位或权力确实存在并有效
senses.example: The government acknowledged the union's right to strike.
senses.exampleCN: 政府承认了工会罢工的权利。
senses.why: Recognition is the first act of acceptance: once you acknowledge a right, you can no longer pretend it is not there.
senses.whyCN: 认可是接受的第一步：一旦承认某项权利存在，就再也不能假装它不存在。

senses.title: Greet with a small nod
senses.definition: to greet someone with a small movement of the head or a brief smile
senses.definitionCN: 用轻微点头或短暂微笑与人打招呼
senses.example: He acknowledged me with a nod and kept walking.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝我点了点头，继续往前走。
senses.why: A nod is the smallest possible act of recognition, and the word names that physical sign.
senses.whyCN: 点头是最小的一次「认出」，这个词就把这个身体动作收进自己的意思里。

senses.title: Show that you have noticed someone
senses.definition: to show by word or gesture that you have seen a person who is present
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或动作表示你看见了在场的某个人
senses.example: She walked past me without acknowledging me.
senses.exampleCN: 她从我身边走过，完全没有理睬我。
senses.why: Not acknowledging someone is a deliberate act of not-knowing; the word measures how much recognition a person is given.
senses.whyCN: 不理睬，是故意「装着不认识」；这个词因此也用来衡量一个人得到了多少承认。

senses.title: Be publicly recognized as
senses.definition: to be generally recognized or accepted as having a certain quality or position
senses.definitionCN: 被普遍认可或接受具有某种品质或地位
senses.example: She is widely acknowledged as the finest cellist of her generation.
senses.exampleCN: 她被公认为同代人中最出色的大提琴手。
senses.why: When many people recognize the same thing, private knowledge becomes public standing, and the passive form carries that shared verdict.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人都认出同一件事，私下的了解就成了公开的定评，被动形式承载的正是这份公认。

intro.en: Acknowledge is not a Latin word: it grew out of the Old English verb for knowing, with its ending later rebuilt on the model of knowledge.
intro.cn: acknowledge 不是拉丁词：它从古英语表示「知道」的动词长出来，词尾后来照着 knowledge 的样子重塑。

items.en: The root *ǵneh₃- is generally reconstructed as 'to know'; it also lies behind English know, knowledge and can.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语词根 *ǵneh₃- 表示「知道」；英语的 know、knowledge 与 can 也出自这里。

items.en: Cnāwan meant 'to know, understand', and it is the direct ancestor of the modern verb know.
items.cn: cnāwan 意为「知道、懂得」，是现代动词 know 的直接祖先。

items.en: On- plus cnāwan formed oncnāwan, 'to recognize, perceive, admit'; the prefix added the idea of turning towards something.
items.cn: on- 加 cnāwan 构成 oncnāwan，意为「认出、察觉、承认」；前缀添上「转向某物」的意味。

items.en: The verb became aknowen, 'to admit, confess, recognize', as the prefix weakened to a single a-.
items.cn: 这个动词变成 aknowen，意为「承认、招认、认出」，前缀弱化成一个 a-。

items.en: The modern spelling acknowledge, with its ending modelled on knowledge, appears in the sixteenth century, often dated to the 1550s; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代拼写 acknowledge 的词尾仿照 knowledge 而来，十六世纪出现，通常定在十六世纪五十年代；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the old Germanic root for knowing; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of admitting and confirming.
note.cn: 形近组共享日耳曼语中表示「知道」的老词根；近义组列出其他表示承认与确认的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for what a person knows; its ending reshaped acknowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「知识、了解」，它的词尾重塑了 acknowledge 的拼写。

entries.definition: The basic verb meaning to have knowledge of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「知道、认识」，是最基本的同根词。

entries.definition: Not known or not identified; the old root with a negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未知的、不为人知的」，是老词根加否定前缀。

entries.definition: The noun for an act of admitting, thanking or confirming receipt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认、致谢、收到确认」，是本词加名词后缀而来。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true, often unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认」，常带不情愿的意味。

entries.definition: To admit a fault or a secret, often formally or with emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坦白、招认」，多用于正式或有情绪的场合。

entries.definition: To accept that something exists or is valid; closer to the core of acknowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「认出、承认……有效」，与 acknowledge 的核心义最接近。

entries.definition: To state that something is true or has happened, especially to remove doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「确认、证实」，尤指消除疑虑。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root and the phrases the verb appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用真实的古英语词根，以及这个动词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: The middle of the word is knowledge: to acknowledge is to say that you know.
normal.cn: 词中间藏着 knowledge：acknowledge 就是说出「我知道」。

normal.en: Take away ac- and you have know, the oldest part of the word.
normal.cn: 去掉开头的 ac-，剩下就是 know，这是整个词最古老的部分。

normal.en: Acknowledge receipt is the phrase that runs through offices every day.
normal.cn: acknowledge receipt 是办公室里每天都会出现的说法。

normal.en: Acknowledged as means the crowd has already agreed.
normal.cn: acknowledged as 意味着众人已经一致同意。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the -ledge of knowledge, so the eye reads a word about knowing.
normal.cn: 拼写保留了 knowledge 的 -ledge，眼睛一看就知道这是关于「知道」的词。

abstract.en: Picture a nod across a room: the smallest possible way of saying I know you are here.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着房间点一下头：这是说「我知道你在」的最小方式。

abstract.en: Every sense is one person giving another person a receipt for something: a fact, a fault, a letter, a kindness.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是一个人给另一个人开一张收据：为事实、为过错、为信件、为恩情。

abstract.en: To refuse to acknowledge someone is to remove them from the world you admit to seeing.
abstract.cn: 拒绝理睬一个人，就是把他从你承认看见的世界里划掉。

examples.en: Please acknowledge my email so I know you received it.
examples.cn: 请回复确认你已收到我的邮件，好让我知道。

examples.en: He acknowledged that he had forgotten the appointment.
examples.cn: 他承认自己忘了这个约定。

examples.en: The prize was a way of acknowledging years of quiet work.
examples.cn: 这个奖是对多年默默工作的一种致意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额克闹里吉」——额头上一点，闹哄哄的场面里点个头，就是承认、确认收到。

root: 古英语 oncnāwan「认出、承认」由 on- 加 cnāwan「知道」构成，cnāwan 也是 know 与 knowledge 的来源；中古英语作 aknowen，后来词尾仿 knowledge 改成 -ledge。整个词属日耳曼语来源，没有拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of acknowledge all perform one act: making known that something has registered. What registers may be a fact, a fault, a letter, a kindness, a right, a person in the room, or a shared judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: acknowledge 的八个义项都在做同一件事：让对方知道「这件事我已登记」。被登记的可能是一个事实、一个过错、一封信、一份恩情、一项权利、房间里的一个人，或一个共同的评判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nod that says I have seen and registered this.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个点头，表示我看见了，也记下了。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: what is already known is spoken aloud, first as fact and then as fault.
branches.cn: 真相线：心里已知的事被说出口，先是事实，后是过错。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: recognition shrinks to a receipt when a letter or payment arrives.
branches.cn: 消息线：当信件或款项抵达，「认出」缩成一张收据。

branches.en: THE DEBT: to recognize help is to admit that something is owed.
branches.cn: 恩情线：承认帮助，也就是承认自己欠着一份情。

branches.en: THE STANDING: a right, a rank or a reputation is accepted by enough people to become real.
branches.cn: 地位线：一项权利、一个身份或一份名声，被足够多的人接受才成为现实。

branches.en: THE BODY: a nod, or the refusal to nod, shows how much recognition a person is given.
branches.cn: 身体线：点一下头，或拒绝点头，显示出一个人被给予了多少承认。

intro.en: Acknowledge is built from Old English pieces, and English suffixes extend the family.
intro.cn: acknowledge 由古英语的成分搭成，英语后缀再把这个词族扩展开。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor, so there are no Latin cognates to list here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，因此这里没有可列出的拉丁同源词。

items.example: It gave oncnāwan the sense of turning towards something.
items.exampleCN: 它让 oncnāwan 带上「转向某物」的意味。

items.example: Cnāwan is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: cnāwan 是这个词最古老的一层。

items.example: The modern verb descends from cnāwan.
items.exampleCN: 现代动词由 cnāwan 传下来。

items.example: Its ending reshaped the spelling of acknowledge.
items.exampleCN: 它的词尾重塑了 acknowledge 的拼写。

items.example: Its origin is not fully certain, but it survives in knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 它的来源不完全确定，但保存在 knowledge 里。

items.example: It is the worn-down form of on- in aknowen.
items.exampleCN: 它是 aknowen 中 on- 磨损后的形式。
它构成 unacknowledged。
它构成 acknowledged。
它构成 acknowledgment。

definition_zh: 获得；获取；习得；收购；染上
definition_en: to get or gain something, especially by effort, purchase or experience
core_image: 伸手去够，够了几次，终于把想要的东西拿到自己这边
scene: 她在国外住了两年，回来时已经能说一口当地话。Children acquire language faster than adults.
sceneCN: 这里 acquire 指在生活环境中自然学会一门语言（第 2 个义项：通过练习习得技能或语言）；句意为孩子习得语言比成年人快。

pos.zh: 动词：获得；获取；习得；收购；染上

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -sition 构成，义为「获取；收购；习得」
由本词加 -itive 构成，义为「贪求的；渴望占有的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「获得者；收购方」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「可获得的；可学会的」

senses.title: Obtain something by effort or payment
senses.definition: to get something, especially by working for it or by paying for it
senses.definitionCN: 得到某物，尤指通过努力或付钱取得
senses.example: They saved for years to acquire the small flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们攒了好几年钱才买下那套小公寓。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to seek, and the prefix added 'in addition'; what you have sought and gained comes to rest on your side.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「寻求」，前缀又加上「额外、到手」的意思；寻求并且得手的东西，就停到了你这一边。

senses.title: Gain a skill or language through practice
senses.definition: to learn a skill, habit or language gradually, especially by using it
senses.definitionCN: 逐步学会某种技能、习惯或语言，尤指在使用中学会
senses.example: Children acquire language faster than adults.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子习得语言比成年人快。
senses.why: A skill is not handed over; it is sought again and again until it stays with you, so the seeking verb covers learning.
senses.whyCN: 技能不是别人递过来的，而是一次次去够，直到它留在你身上；于是「寻求」这个动词也覆盖了「学会」。

senses.title: Buy or take over a company
senses.definition: to buy a company or a large share of it, or to gain control of it
senses.definitionCN: 买下一家公司或其很大一部分股份，或取得其控制权
senses.example: The chain acquired three smaller rivals last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁企业去年收购了三家较小的对手。
senses.why: A company is simply a very large object of purchase, and the old verb of getting takes on the cool tone of business.
senses.whyCN: 一家公司无非是一件非常大的可购之物，「取得」这个老动词于是带上了商业的冷静口气。

senses.title: Come to like something gradually
senses.definition: to develop a liking for something, especially in the phrase acquire a taste for
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐对某物产生喜爱，尤用于短语 acquire a taste for
senses.example: He acquired a taste for black coffee during his years abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外那几年，他慢慢喜欢上了黑咖啡。
senses.why: Liking, too, can be something you come to possess: it arrives by repeated exposure, like an object slowly carried home.
senses.whyCN: 喜好也可以是一件「得到」的东西：它靠反复接触慢慢到来，像一件被一点点搬回家的物件。

senses.title: Gain knowledge or information
senses.definition: to get knowledge, information or data, often by searching or collecting it
senses.definitionCN: 获得知识、信息或数据，常通过查找与收集
senses.example: The team acquired enough data to test the theory.
senses.exampleCN: 团队获取了足够的数据来检验这个理论。
senses.why: Information is what you go out and seek; the word keeps the original hunt inside the modern lab.
senses.whyCN: 信息正是你出去寻找的东西；这个词把原始的「搜寻」保留在现代实验室里。

senses.title: Come to have a reputation or quality
senses.definition: to develop a reputation, label or quality over time, often without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间形成某种名声、标签或特征，常非有意为之
senses.example: The street acquired a reputation for cheap food and loud music.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街渐渐有了「吃食便宜、音乐吵闹」的名声。
senses.why: A reputation is not bought; it accumulates around a person or place until it belongs to them, and the word treats it as a possession.
senses.whyCN: 名声不是买来的，它围绕一个人或一个地方累积，直到归其所有；这个词便把它当成一份所有物。

senses.title: Catch a disease or condition
senses.definition: to become infected with a disease, or to develop a condition such as immunity
senses.definitionCN: 感染某种疾病，或形成免疫力之类的状态
senses.example: Patients can acquire the infection during a long hospital stay.
senses.exampleCN: 病人可能在长期住院期间染上这种感染。
senses.why: Illness is something that comes to settle in the body without being invited, so even a thing you do not want is 'acquired'.
senses.whyCN: 疾病是不请自来、在身体里住下的东西，所以连你不想要的东西也会被说成「获得」。

senses.title: Gained after birth, not inherited
senses.definition: of a quality or condition, developed during life rather than present from birth
senses.definitionCN: 指某种品质或状况在生命过程中形成，而非与生俱来
senses.example: The doctor explained the difference between inherited and acquired traits.
senses.exampleCN: 医生解释了遗传特征与后天特征的区别。
senses.why: Science needed a word for what is added to an organism after it starts, and the old verb of getting supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个词来指「生命开始之后才添上去」的东西，而那个表示「取得」的老动词正好提供了它。

intro.en: Acquire is a Latin verb of seeking, with a prefix that means 'to' or 'in addition', carried into English through Old French.
intro.cn: acquire 是一个表示「寻求」的拉丁语动词，带一个意为「朝向、额外」的前缀，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Quaerere meant 'to seek, search for, ask'; the same verb lies behind inquire, require, question and query.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、搜寻、询问」；inquire、require、question 与 query 都出自同一个动词。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant 'to, towards'. Before q it was written ac-, so ad plus quaerere appears as acquirere.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向、朝」。在 q 之前写作 ac-，因此 ad 加 quaerere 写作 acquirere。

items.en: Acquirere meant 'to get in addition, procure, gain'; its past participle acquisitus is the base of acquisition.
items.cn: acquirere 意为「额外获得、取得、得到」；其过去分词 acquisitus 是 acquisition 的基础。

items.en: Old French aquerre carried the verb towards English, and Middle English borrowed it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 aquerre 把这个动词带向英语，中古英语在十五世纪借入。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain, and the business sense 'buy a company' belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 这个动词自十五世纪有记录；确切首见年代不确定，而「收购公司」的商业义属于二十世纪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin verb of seeking; the near-meaning group lists other ways of getting something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语「寻求」动词构成的一族词；近义组列出其他表示「得到」的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of getting something, especially a company or a skill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获取、收购、习得」，尤指公司或技能。

entries.definition: To need something or demand it as necessary; the same Latin verb with re-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「需要、要求」，是同一拉丁动词加 re- 构成。

entries.definition: To ask for information; literally to seek into something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「询问、打听」，字面意思是「往里寻求」。

entries.definition: To declare someone not guilty; it only looks similar and comes from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣判无罪」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To get something, especially by effort; more formal than acquire and common with permissions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，比 acquire 更正式，常与许可、批准搭配。

entries.definition: To get something useful or valuable over time, such as experience or weight.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赢得、增加」，多指随着时间得到有用的东西，如经验或体重。

entries.definition: To obtain something with effort, often through a supplier or a formal process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设法取得」，常通过供应商或正式程序，语气正式。

entries.definition: To get money or respect in return for work or good conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挣得、赢得」，强调以工作或品行换取。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of seeking and the phrases acquire appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用真实的拉丁语「寻求」动词，以及 acquire 常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Quaerere means to seek: acquire is what happens when the seeking ends in your hands.
normal.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求」：acquire 就是寻求结束时东西落在你手里。

normal.en: Inquire, require and acquire all hide the same quaerere.
normal.cn: inquire、require、acquire 都藏着同一个 quaerere。

normal.en: Acquire a taste for means the liking itself was slowly obtained.
normal.cn: acquire a taste for 意为连这份喜好也是慢慢得到的。

normal.en: An acquired taste is one you had to work towards.
normal.cn: an acquired taste 是需要你慢慢培养才喜欢的味道。

normal.en: In business, to acquire is simply to buy a whole company.
normal.cn: 在商业里，to acquire 就是买下一整家公司。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for a fruit just out of range, then closing on it: that closing is the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向差一点就够到的果子，然后握住：那一握就是这个词。

abstract.en: Skills, habits, reputations and even illnesses all arrive by the same route: something outside slowly becomes yours.
abstract.cn: 技能、习惯、名声，甚至疾病，都走同一条路：外面的东西慢慢变成你的。

abstract.en: The word is neutral about wanting: you can acquire a fortune or a cold.
abstract.cn: 这个词对「想不想要」保持中立：你可以 acquire 一笔财富，也可以 acquire 一场感冒。

examples.en: Children acquire language faster than adults.
examples.cn: 孩子习得语言比成年人快。

examples.en: They saved for years to acquire the small flat.
examples.cn: 他们攒了好几年钱才买下那套小公寓。

examples.en: He acquired a taste for black coffee during his years abroad.
examples.cn: 在国外那几年，他慢慢喜欢上了黑咖啡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额快儿」——快点伸手去够，够到手就是获得、拿到。

root: 拉丁语 acquirere「额外取得、获得」由 ad-「向」加 quaerere「寻求」构成，ad- 在 q 前写作 ac-；过去分词 acquisitus 生出 acquisition。quaerere 同时也是 inquire、require、question 的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of acquire is the same movement: something outside is sought, reached and then belongs to you. The difference is what is being got, and whether you wanted it.
sensesIntro.cn: acquire 的每个义项都是同一个动作：外面的东西被寻求、被够到，然后归你所有。区别只在于得到的是什么，以及那是不是你想要的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out and closing on something it has been seeking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸出去，把一直在找的东西握住。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: from a small purchase to a whole company, the word covers what can be got.
branches.cn: 物件线：从小件购买到整家公司，这个词覆盖一切能取得的东西。

branches.en: THE MIND: skills, languages and information are got by seeking them repeatedly.
branches.cn: 心智线：技能、语言与信息，都靠反复寻求才到手。

branches.en: THE APPETITE: even a liking can be slowly obtained, as in acquire a taste for.
branches.cn: 口味线：连喜好也能慢慢获得，如 acquire a taste for。

branches.en: THE UNINVITED: reputation and disease settle on a person without being asked for.
branches.cn: 不请自来线：名声与疾病未经邀请就落在一个人身上。

branches.en: THE TIMING: whatever is added after birth rather than inherited is marked as acquired.
branches.cn: 时间线：凡是出生之后才添上、而非遗传而来的，都标为后天的。

intro.en: Acquire is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb of seeking, and English builds its family with ordinary endings.
intro.cn: acquire 是一个拉丁语前缀加一个表示「寻求」的拉丁语动词，英语用普通词尾扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Quaerere, acquirere and their forms are recorded Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: quaerere、acquirere 及其形式都是有记录的拉丁语，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 它把「寻求」指向某个对象。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 acquirere 与 acquire 里。

items.example: Quaerere is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是这个词的核心。

items.example: Acquirere is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: acquirere 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: They acquired the land in stages.
items.exampleCN: 他们分阶段取得了这块地。

definition_zh: 横过；穿过；在……对面；遍及；跨越
definition_en: from one side of something to the other, on the opposite side, or throughout an area
core_image: 一条横线从纸的左岸划到右岸，中间不绕路
scene: 雨下得正急，她把书包顶在头上冲过马路去赶公交。She ran across the street to catch the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 across 指从马路一边到另一边（第 1 个义项：横过、穿过）；句意为她跑过马路去赶公交车。

pos.zh: 介词：横过；在……对面；遍及
副词：横过；在对面；宽

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 from 构成的短语介词，义为「在……对面」
由本词与 board 复合构成，义为「全面的；影响到所有人的」

senses.title: From one side to the other
senses.definition: moving or reaching from one side of a road, river, room or line to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从道路、河流、房间或界线的一边移到或延伸到另一边
senses.example: She ran across the street to catch the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 她跑过马路去赶公交车。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning 'in a cross', and a cross is exactly the line that goes from one side to the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「成十字形」的短语，而十字正是从一边横到另一边的那条线。

senses.title: On the opposite side
senses.definition: on the other side of a road, river or space, seen from where you stand
senses.definitionCN: 从你所站的位置看，位于道路、河流或空地的另一边
senses.example: The bakery is just across the road from our flat.
senses.exampleCN: 那家面包店就在我们公寓的马路对面。
senses.why: Once the crossing is finished, the same word describes where you have arrived: the far side.
senses.whyCN: 一旦横过去，这个词就转而描述你抵达的那一边：对面。

senses.title: Spanning from one side to the other
senses.definition: extending over something, as a bridge extends over a river or a smile spreads over a face
senses.definitionCN: 横着延伸覆盖某物，如桥横跨河面、笑容在脸上展开
senses.example: A new bridge was built across the river last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年河上建起了一座新桥。
senses.why: A bridge is a crossing frozen in place, so the moving word becomes a word for what spans.
senses.whyCN: 桥是一座被固定住的横越，于是这个表示动作的词也用来指「横跨在那里的东西」。

senses.title: Throughout an area or group
senses.definition: in every part of a place, or among all the members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地方的每个部分，或一个群体的所有成员之中
senses.example: Small cafés like this are found across the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的咖啡馆遍布全城。
senses.why: If you cross a whole region in your mind, the crossing leaves the word spread over its surface instead of at one point.
senses.whyCN: 如果在心里横越整个地区，这条越过的线就把词铺满它的表面，而不是停在一点上。

senses.title: Come across: find by chance
senses.definition: in the phrase come across, to meet or find someone or something without planning to
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 come across，指没有计划地遇到或发现某人某物
senses.example: I came across an old photo while cleaning the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 我清理抽屉时偶然翻到一张旧照片。
senses.why: Walking across a space, you pass things you did not set out to find; the crossing becomes the chance meeting.
senses.whyCN: 走过一片空间时，你会经过原本没打算找的东西；这条横越的路就成了那场偶遇。

senses.title: Get across: make understood
senses.definition: in the phrase get across, to succeed in making an idea or feeling understood by others
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 get across，指成功让别人理解某个想法或感受
senses.example: He struggled to get his point across in the noisy meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 在吵闹的会上，他费了很大劲才把观点讲清楚。
senses.why: An idea has to travel from one mind to another, and across is the shortest picture of that crossing.
senses.whyCN: 想法必须从一个头脑传到另一个头脑，而 across 正是对这次越渡最简短的描画。

senses.title: Across the board: affecting everyone
senses.definition: in the phrase across the board, applying to all people, levels or cases without exception
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 across the board，指适用于所有人、所有层级或所有情况，没有例外
senses.example: Prices went up across the board this month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个月各类价格全面上涨。
senses.why: A line drawn across a board cuts every column at once, and the phrase keeps that image of one sweep covering all.
senses.whyCN: 在板上横划一道线，会同时切过每一栏；这个短语保留了「一扫而过、全部覆盖」的画面。

senses.title: Measured in width
senses.definition: used after a measurement to say how wide something is from side to side
senses.definitionCN: 用在度量之后，表示某物从一边到另一边有多宽
senses.example: The pool is twenty metres across at its widest point.
senses.exampleCN: 泳池最宽处有二十米宽。
senses.why: Width is the distance a crossing would cover, so the word of crossing also measures the space between the two sides.
senses.whyCN: 宽度正是一次横越要覆盖的距离，因此表示横越的词也用来量两边之间的空间。

intro.en: Across began as an English phrase meaning 'in a cross', built on the Latin word for a cross that also gave cross, crucial and crusade.
intro.cn: across 最初是一个意为「成十字形」的英语短语，建立在拉丁语「十字」一词之上；cross、crucial 与 crusade 也同出此源。

items.en: Crux meant 'cross', and also 'a torture frame'. It is the source of cross, crucial, crusade and the English noun crux.
items.cn: crux 意为「十字」，也指「刑架」。它是 cross、crucial、crusade 以及英语名词 crux 的来源。

items.en: Old French croix meant 'cross', and phrases such as a croix or en croix meant 'in the form of a cross'.
items.cn: 古法语 croix 意为「十字」，a croix 或 en croix 之类的短语意为「成十字形」。

items.en: The phrase was written together as across, first meaning 'in the form of a cross, crossing', then 'from side to side'. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个短语被连写成一个词 across，先表示「成十字形、交叉」，再表示「从一边到另一边」。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The preposition and adverb uses settled: a road could be crossed, and a person could stand across from another.
items.cn: 介词与副词用法逐渐固定：路可以被横过，人也可以站在另一个人的对面。

items.en: The word spread into figurative patterns: across the country, across the board, come across and get across.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到比喻用法：across the country、across the board、come across 与 get across。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin cross behind across; the near-meaning group gathers other prepositions of position and movement.
note.cn: 形近组共享 across 背后那个拉丁语「十字」；近义组列出其他表示位置与移动的介词。

entries.definition: A noun and verb for a shape of two lines, or for going from one side to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 名词兼动词，义为「十字；横过」，与 across 同出拉丁语 crux。

entries.definition: A place where a road or river may be crossed, or the act of crossing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十字路口、渡口」或「横越的行为」。

entries.definition: A phrase meaning directly opposite something.
entries.definitionCN: 短语介词，义为「在……正对面」，由本词加 from 构成。

entries.definition: Extremely important, from a Latin word for a cross and the idea of a deciding point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「至关重要的」，源自拉丁语「十字」以及「决定性的岔口」这一意象。

entries.definition: Above something, or from one side to the other, especially by going above it.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……上方」或「越过」，尤指从上方过去。

entries.definition: From one end or side to the other, by passing inside something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「穿过」，强调从内部通过。

entries.definition: On the far side of something, or further than a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……那一边」或「超出」。

entries.definition: Facing something from the other side; close to the 'opposite side' sense of across.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或形容词，义为「在……对面」，与 across 的「对面」义最接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin cross and the fixed phrases across appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用真实的拉丁语「十字」，以及 across 常出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: The hidden noun is cross: across means in the shape of a cross, from side to side.
normal.cn: 藏在里面的名词是 cross：across 就是成十字形、从一边到另一边。

normal.en: Latin crux gives cross, crucial, crusade and crucify.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 crux 生出 cross、crucial、crusade 与 crucify。

normal.en: Come across is a crossing that happens by chance.
normal.cn: come across 是一次碰巧发生的横越。

normal.en: Get across is an idea crossing from one head to another.
normal.cn: get across 是一个想法从上一个人的头脑横越到另一个。

normal.en: Across the board means one line cuts every column.
normal.cn: across the board 意为一条横线切过每一栏。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn across a page: it starts at one edge and stops at the other, touching everything in between.
abstract.cn: 想象一条横过纸面的线：从一边起笔，到另一边停住，中间的一切都被它掠过。

abstract.en: The same line explains the opposite side, the whole city, a bridge and a rumour that spreads everywhere.
abstract.cn: 同一条线也解释了「对面」「全城」、一座桥，以及到处传开的传闻。

abstract.en: A crossing always leaves two banks behind, which is why the word cares about both sides at once.
abstract.cn: 一次横越总会留下两岸，所以这个词同时在意两边。

examples.en: She ran across the street to catch the bus.
examples.cn: 她跑过马路去赶公交车。

examples.en: The bakery is just across the road from our flat.
examples.cn: 那家面包店就在我们公寓的马路对面。

examples.en: He struggled to get his point across in the noisy meeting.
examples.cn: 在吵闹的会上，他费了很大劲才把观点讲清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额克绕死」——绕来绕去也要横过马路，到对面去。

root: 中古英语 across 由 a（弱化的 on）加 crois「十字」连写而成，crois 来自古法语，源头是拉丁语 crux「十字、刑架」；cross、crucial、crusade 与 crucify 都同出此源。

sensesIntro.en: Across always draws a line between two sides. Whether the line is a road crossed on foot, the far bank, a bridge, a whole region, a chance meeting, an idea, a board or a width depends on what it touches.
sensesIntro.cn: across 始终在两边之间画一条线。这条线是走过的马路、对岸、桥、整个地区、一次偶遇、一个想法、一块板，还是一段宽度，取决于它落到的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn from one edge of a page to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从纸的一边直划到另一边的线。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT: a body or a bridge goes from one side to the other.
branches.cn: 移动线：身体或桥梁从一边到了另一边。

branches.en: THE POSITION: after the crossing, the far side becomes the place where you are or look.
branches.cn: 位置线：横越之后，另一边成了你所在或所看的地方。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: a line drawn over a region covers every part of it.
branches.cn: 铺展线：一条划过地区的线，覆盖了它的每个部分。

branches.en: THE ACCIDENT: crossing a space brings chance meetings, and crossing between minds carries ideas.
branches.cn: 偶遇线：横越一片空间会带来偶遇，而头脑之间的横越则运送想法。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: one sweep covers all columns, and the same span becomes a width measured in metres.
branches.cn: 度量线：一扫覆盖所有栏目，而同一段跨度又成了以米衡量的宽度。

intro.en: Across is an English phrase fused into one word, built on a French form of the Latin noun for a cross.
intro.cn: across 是一个融合成单词的英语短语，建立在拉丁语「十字」名词的法语形式之上。

latinIntro.en: Crux and its derivatives are recorded Latin; the fused English phrase is the later layer.
latinIntro.cn: crux 及其派生形式都是有记录的拉丁语，融合成单词的英语短语属于更晚的一层。

items.exampleCN: 它是旧短语中磨损后的 on。

items.example: Crois is the French form of Latin crux.
items.exampleCN: crois 是拉丁语 crux 的法语形式。

items.example: Crux is the ultimate source of across.
items.exampleCN: crux 是 across 的最终来源。

items.meaning: a cross shape; to go over
items.example: Cross and across share one origin.
items.exampleCN: cross 与 across 同出一源。

items.example: The image is a fork in the road.

definition_zh: 行为；举动；表演；法案；幕；（戏剧等的）节目；行动；起作用
definition_en: to do something, to behave in a certain way, to perform, or to have an effect; also a deed, a law, or a division of a play
core_image: 舞台中央一个人抬手、转身、开口，一个动作被所有人看见
scene: 剧场里灯光暗下来，导演在幕后低声数着节拍。The young man acted the part of a nervous bridegroom.
sceneCN: 这里的 acted 是「表演、扮演」（第 3 个义项：在舞台或银幕上演一个角色）；句意为那个年轻人演了一个紧张的新郎。

pos.zh: 行动；举止表现；表演；起作用
行为；法案；幕；表演节目

derivatives.zh: 由 act 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「行动；动作；作用；诉讼」
由 act 加表示施动者的 -or 构成，义为「演员；行动者」
由 act 加 -ing 构成，义为「表演；演技」，也可作形容词表示「代理的」
