entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现、使成为现实」，建立在同一个形容词之上。

entries.definition: In fact or truly; closer to plain emphasis and less often used for polite correction.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「真正地、确实」，更偏向单纯强调，较少用于委婉纠正。

entries.definition: Sincerely or genuinely; more formal and warmer than actually.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「真诚地、确实」，比 actually 更正式也更有温度。

entries.definition: In the exact sense of the words, not figuratively; it tests wording rather than facts.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「字面意义上地」，检验的是措辞而非事实。

entries.definition: In practice or almost; it can soften a claim instead of asserting the fact.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上、几乎」，常用于弱化说法，而非断言事实。

entries.definition: Used to confirm or strengthen a statement, often after the listener has spoken.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「确实、的确」，多用于确认或加强对方刚说过的话。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the adjective behind the adverb, the older sense and the conversational jobs the word does.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借助副词背后的形容词、它较早的那层意思，以及它在口语里承担的各种功能。

normal.en: Actual means real, and -ly turns it into the adverb that points at what is real.
normal.cn: actual 意为「真实的」，-ly 把它变成指向「真实」的副词。

normal.en: The oldest sense was 'actively'; the sense 'in fact' is a later shift.
normal.cn: 最早的意思是「积极地」；「事实上」是后来才发生的转变。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence, actually usually softens a correction.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，actually 通常是在缓和一句纠正。

normal.en: In the middle of a sentence with stress, it marks surprise: he actually said yes.
normal.cn: 在句中重读时，它标记惊讶：he actually said yes。

normal.en: In a question, it turns doubt into a direct challenge.
normal.cn: 用在疑问句里，它把怀疑变成直接的追问。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper with writing on one side: turn it over and the other side is the truth.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸，一面写着字：翻过来，另一面才是真相。

abstract.en: The same flip can be gentle, as in a polite correction, or sharp, as in a challenge.
abstract.cn: 同一次翻面可以很温和，比如礼貌的纠正；也可以很锋利，比如质问。

abstract.en: Saying actually is always a small claim that the speaker has seen the other side.
abstract.cn: 说出 actually，始终是在小小地声明：说话人已经看过另一面。

examples.en: I thought the shop was closed, but it was actually open.
examples.cn: 我以为那家店关门了，其实它开着。

examples.en: She actually finished the whole report in one night.
examples.cn: 她竟然一个晚上就把整份报告写完了。

examples.en: Actually, I have never been to that part of town.
examples.cn: 其实我从来没去过城里的那一片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克雀利」——嘴上说的先别信，翻过来看另一面：实际上。

root: 由 actual 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；actual 出自晚期拉丁语 actualis「活跃的、实际的」，其词根 actus 是 agere「驱动、做」的过去分词。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb always points to the other side of what was said: a reality against an appearance, a fact added, a surprise, an emphasis, a soft correction, a new topic, a challenge, or an older sense of 'now'.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词始终指向「说法的另一面」：与表象相对的真实、补充的事实、意外、强调、委婉的纠正、新的话题、质问，或较早的「此刻」之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper turned over to show the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸被翻过来，露出另一面。

branches.en: THE FLIP: what seems to be the case is set against what is the case.
branches.cn: 翻面线：看起来的样子被放在真实情况的对立面。

branches.en: THE FACT: the word either supplies the fact or presses on it until the listener believes it.
branches.cn: 事实线：这个词要么补上事实，要么把事实按到听者相信为止。

branches.en: THE JOLT: reality can arrive as surprise in a statement or as doubt in a question.
branches.cn: 冲击线：现实可以是陈述里的惊讶，也可以是疑问里的怀疑。

branches.en: THE CONVERSATION: the same marker manages disagreement and changes of subject.
branches.cn: 对话线：同一个标记既管理分歧，也管理话题的转换。

branches.en: THE OLD LAYER: before it meant 'in fact', the word meant 'in action, now'.
branches.cn: 旧层线：在表示「事实上」之前，这个词的意思是「在行动中、此刻」。

intro.en: Actually is the adjective actual plus the adverb suffix -ly; the base itself is a Latin adjective on the act root.
intro.cn: actually 是形容词 actual 加副词后缀 -ly；而这个词基本身是建立在 act 词根上的拉丁形容词。

latinIntro.en: Agere, actus and actualis are recorded Latin forms; the Indo-European root above them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: agere、actus 与 actualis 都是有文献记录的拉丁语形式；更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The root lies behind Latin agere.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根藏在拉丁语 agere 之后。

items.example: Agere is the ultimate source of the family.
items.exampleCN: agere 是这一词族的最初来源。

items.example: Actus is the noun behind actualis.
items.exampleCN: actus 是 actualis 背后的名词。
actualis 给出了英语的 actual。

items.example: Actually is built directly on this adjective.
items.exampleCN: actually 直接建立在这个形容词之上。
它把 actual 变成 actually。
它构成 actuality。
它构成 actualize。

definition_zh: 适应；使适应；改编；改装；改造
definition_en: to change your behaviour or to change something else so that it fits new conditions, a new purpose, or a different audience
core_image: 一件原本合身的外套被改了几针，穿到另一个身形上又合身了
scene: 外婆搬进城里的小公寓，阳台朝北，她把旧藤椅挪了三次才坐得舒服。She soon adapted to life in the small apartment.
sceneCN: 这里 adapt 是「适应新的生活条件」（第 1 个义项：人为适应新环境而改变自己的做法）；句意为她很快就适应了小公寓里的生活。

pos.zh: 动词：适应；使适应；改编；改装；改造

不及物动词：适应（常与 to 连用）

senses.title: Of a person: to fit into new conditions
senses.definition: to change your habits, behaviour or way of living so that you can live or work well in new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改变习惯、做法或生活方式，以便在新的条件下顺利生活或工作
senses.example: It took her a month to adapt to the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个月才适应夜班。
senses.why: The Latin root aptus means fit; ad- adds toward, so the verb is literally to make oneself fitting for a situation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 aptus 意为「合适」，前缀 ad- 表示「朝向」，所以这个动词本义就是「把自己调整到与情境相合」。

senses.title: Of a species: to become suited to its habitat
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, to develop features over generations that make survival in a particular environment more likely
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物经过许多代发展出某些特征，使其更容易在特定环境中存活
senses.example: These birds adapted to the colder coast within a few generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟在几代之内就适应了更寒冷的海岸。
senses.why: The same idea of fitting is stretched over time: what is fitted is not one body but a whole population and its surroundings.
senses.whyCN: 「合适」这层意思被拉长到时间尺度上：被调整到相合的不再是一个身体，而是整个种群与它的环境。

senses.title: Of the eyes: to adjust to light or dark
senses.definition: of the eyes or another sense organ, to become able to see or feel clearly after a change of light or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指眼睛等感觉器官在光线或环境改变后逐渐恢复清晰的感知
senses.example: Wait a moment while your eyes adapt to the darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 稍等一下，让眼睛适应黑暗。
senses.why: The fitting here happens inside the body and takes only seconds: the eye tunes itself until the image is clear again.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「相合」发生在身体内部，只消几秒：眼睛自行调整到图像重新清晰为止。

senses.title: To alter an object for a new use
senses.definition: to change the design or parts of an object so that it can be used for a different purpose
senses.definitionCN: 改变物体的设计或部件，使其能用于另一种用途
senses.example: He adapted an old coffee tin into a lamp holder.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一个旧咖啡罐改装成了灯座。
senses.why: If a thing must fit a new job, it is altered until it does; the object, not the person, is the one that changes.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件东西要胜任新用途，就把它改到合适为止；这里改变的是物，而不是人。

senses.title: To rewrite a story for screen or stage
senses.definition: to turn a book, play or other written work into a film, television series or stage production
senses.definitionCN: 把书、戏剧或其他文字作品改成电影、电视剧或舞台作品
senses.example: The studio adapted the novel into a six-part series.
senses.exampleCN: 制片方把那部小说改编成了六集剧集。
senses.why: A story written for one medium must be cut and reshaped until it fits another; the fit is between forms, not bodies.
senses.whyCN: 为一个媒介写的故事要经过删改与重塑，才能与另一个媒介相合；这里的「合身」发生在两种形式之间，与身体无关。

senses.title: To adjust lessons to a group of learners
senses.titleCN: 调整（教材、课程）以适合学习者
senses.definition: to change teaching materials, tasks or courses so that they suit the level and needs of a particular class
senses.definitionCN: 修改教材、任务或课程，使其适合某个班级的水平与需要
senses.example: Good teachers adapt the same worksheet for weaker classes.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师会把同一份练习改编给基础较弱的班级。
senses.why: The material is not wrong; it simply has to be fitted to the people using it, the same way clothes are taken in or let out.
senses.whyCN: 材料本身没有错，只是要量着使用者的身量改一改，就像衣服改肥改瘦。

senses.title: To modify a building or vehicle for disabled users
senses.titleCN: 改造（建筑、车辆）以便无障碍使用
senses.definition: to change a building, vehicle or piece of equipment so that people with disabilities can use it
senses.definitionCN: 改造建筑、车辆或设备，使残障人士也能使用
senses.example: The museum adapted its main entrance for wheelchair users.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆改造了正门，方便轮椅使用者出入。
senses.why: Here the fitting has a fixed shape in mind: the design is bent until a specific body can get through.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「相合」有一个明确的身体作参照：把设计改到某类身体也能通过为止。

senses.title: To change your manner to suit other people
senses.titleCN: 调整言谈举止以适合场合或对象
senses.definition: to change the way you speak or behave so that it suits a particular person, group or social occasion
senses.definitionCN: 改变说话或行事的方式，使之适合特定的人、群体或社交场合
senses.example: A good host adapts his tone to the guests at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 好的主人会按同桌客人的不同来调整自己的语气。
senses.why: What is fitted now is the self: the manner is adjusted the way a garment is, until it sits well in the room.
senses.whyCN: 这时被调整的就是自己：言谈像衣服一样被改到在场合里看着得体。

intro.en: Adapt is a Latin verb built from ad- and aptare, and English took it over in the sixteenth century with the idea of fitting already inside it.
intro.cn: adapt 是由拉丁语前缀 ad- 与动词 aptare 构成的，英语在十六世纪借入时，「使相合」的意思已经包含在里面。

items.en: Aptus meant 'fitted, suitable, apt'. It is generally connected with the verb apere, 'to fasten, attach', but the deeper origin of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: aptus 意为「合适的、恰当的」，一般认为与动词 apere「系上、连接」有关，但这个词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: From aptus came the verb aptare, 'to fit, fasten, adjust', used of clothes, armour and equipment as well as of abstract matters.
items.cn: 由 aptus 生出动词 aptare，意为「使合适、系紧、调整」，既用于衣物、盔甲与装备，也用于抽象事物。

items.en: The prefix ad-, 'to, toward', plus aptare produced adaptare, 'to fit to, make suitable for'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 表示「朝向」，与 aptare 合成 adaptare，意为「使合于、使适合于」。

items.en: English borrowed the word as adapt, first in the sense 'to fit or suit', and the spelling has been stable since then.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 adapt，最初义为「使相合、使适合」，此后拼写基本未变。

items.en: The biological sense 'to become suited to a habitat' spread in the nineteenth century, and the film and stage sense of adapting a work in the twentieth.
items.cn: 「适应栖息环境」的生物学义在十九世纪流行开来，「改编作品」的影视与舞台义则在二十世纪扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family built on aptus plus one accidental twin; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of adjusting, modifying and tailoring.
note.cn: 形近组收以 aptus 为根的一族词，外加一个纯属拼写相近的词；近义组收调整、修改与量体裁衣一类的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of fitting something to new conditions, or for a work rewritten for another medium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编、改编作品」，指使某物合于新条件的行为，或为另一媒介改写的作品。

entries.definition: Able to change easily in order to suit new conditions; formed with the suffix -able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能适应的、可改装的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A device that lets one plug or part fit another, or a person who rewrites a work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适配器、转接头」，也指改编者；由本词加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Very skilled at something; it looks close to adapt but comes from Latin adeptus, a person who has attained something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟练的、内行的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它出自拉丁语 adeptus「已达到者」。

entries.definition: To change something slightly, often a machine or a position, so that it works or looks right.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整、校准」，多指小幅改动机器或位置，使之正常或合适。

entries.definition: To change something in part, usually to improve it; more deliberate and formal than adapt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改、改进」，通常指部分改动，比 adapt 更有计划性、语气更正式。

entries.definition: To change your plans or arrangements so that someone's needs are met.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「迁就、顾及」，指改变安排以满足某人的需要。

entries.definition: To make or change something for a particular person or purpose, as a tailor cuts cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「量身定制、按需调整」，像裁缝裁布一样为特定的人或目的改动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin base aptus and the three patterns the verb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词基 aptus，以及这个动词实际出现的三种结构。

normal.en: Aptus is Latin for fitted, so adapt is what you do until something is fitted to its situation.
normal.cn: aptus 在拉丁语里就是「合适的」，adapt 就是一直改到某物与情境相合。

normal.en: The prefix ad- means toward, so the fitting is always pointed at someone or something.
normal.cn: 前缀 ad- 表示「朝向」，所以这种「合适」总是朝着某人或某物而去。

normal.en: Adapt to a place, adapt something for a person, and adapt a book from a novel are the three common patterns.
normal.cn: 接 to 说环境，接 for 说对象，接 from 说来源，是三种常见结构。

normal.en: Adaptation, adaptable and adapter all keep the same Latin base.
normal.cn: adaptation、adaptable、adapter 都保留同一个拉丁词基。

normal.en: In biology a species adapts; in film a studio adapts a novel; both fit one thing to another.
normal.cn: 生物学里物种 adapt，电影圈里制片方 adapt 一部小说，两者都是把一个东西改到与另一个相合。

abstract.en: Picture a jacket taken in at the waist: the person has not changed, the jacket has.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套在腰间被收了几针：人没变，变的是外套。

abstract.en: Fit is a relation, not a quality: the same key opens one door and fails at the next.
abstract.cn: 「合」是一种关系，不是一种属性：同一把钥匙开得了这扇门，却开不了下一扇。

abstract.en: Every new place asks the same question: what here must be altered, the world or me?
abstract.cn: 每到一个新地方都在问同一个问题：要改的是这里的东西，还是我自己？

examples.en: My parents adapted quickly to video calls.
examples.cn: 我爸妈很快就适应了视频通话。

examples.en: The director adapted the book for a younger audience.
examples.cn: 导演把这本书改编成了适合年轻观众看的版本。

examples.en: We adapted the spare room into a small office.
examples.cn: 我们把那间空房改成了小办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鹅大夫特」——鹅大夫特别会随环境换法子，旧衣改一改就合身：适应、改装。

root: 拉丁语 aptus「合适的」加前缀 ad-「朝向」，先有 aptare「使合适」，再合成 adaptare「使合于」。aptus 一般认为与 apere「系上、连接」有关，更早来源不确定；英语于十六世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses apply one adjustment to a different thing: a person, a species, the eyes, an object, a story, a lesson, a building, or a manner of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项做的是同一件事——一次调整，只是被调整的东西不同：人、物种、眼睛、物件、故事、课程、建筑，或说话的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a garment is taken in a little, and it now sits on a different body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件衣服被收了收针脚，便合上了另一个身形。

branches.en: THE PERSON: habits are altered until daily life in a new place runs smoothly.
branches.cn: 人线：改的是习惯，直到在新地方的日子顺起来。

branches.en: THE BODY: a population changes over generations, and the eye changes in seconds.
branches.cn: 身体线：种群用许多代来改变，眼睛只用几秒。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a tin, a car or a doorway is rebuilt until a new use fits it.
branches.cn: 物件线：罐子、车辆或门口被改造到能容纳新用途。

branches.en: THE TEXT: a story or a worksheet is reshaped until another audience can take it in.
branches.cn: 文本线：故事或练习被重塑到另一批读者或学生接得住。

branches.en: THE SELF: the last thing fitted is your own tone of voice.
branches.cn: 自我线：最后被调整的，是你自己的语气。

intro.en: Adapt is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb of fitting, and English builds its family with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: adapt 由一个拉丁前缀和一个表示「使合适」的拉丁动词构成，英语再用普通后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Aptus, aptare and adaptare are all recorded in Latin, so only the deeper root behind aptus is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: aptus、aptare 与 adaptare 在拉丁语中均有记录，只有 aptus 背后更早的词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix directs the fitting toward something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「使合适」这个动作指向某个对象。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整个词族的词基。

items.example: It was used of clothes and armour.
items.exampleCN: 这个词曾用于衣物与盔甲。

它构成 adapter。

definition_zh: 添加；增加；加上；补充说；相加
definition_en: to put something together with something else, or to join numbers or words, so that the amount, total or effect becomes greater
core_image: 往已经盛着水的杯子里再倒一勺糖：东西叠上去，分量就变了
scene: 火锅端上桌时汤底还不够辣，朋友拿起辣椒罐又抖了两下。He added more chilli to the soup.
sceneCN: 这里 add 是「添加、放入」（第 1 个义项：把某物放进已有的东西里）；句意为他又往汤里加了辣椒。

pos.zh: 动词：添加；增加；加上；补充说；相加
及物动词：把……加入；把（数字）相加
不及物动词：增添（常与 to 连用）；合计（用于 add up）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ition 构成，义为「添加；增加物；加法」
由名词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「额外的；附加的」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「此外；另外」

由动词与 on 复合而成，义为「附加项；附加设备」

senses.title: To put an ingredient or object into something
senses.definition: to put a substance, ingredient or object into a container or mixture that already has something in it
senses.definitionCN: 把某种物质、配料或物件放进已有东西的容器或混合物中
senses.example: Add a pinch of salt to the boiling water.
senses.exampleCN: 往滚水里加一小撮盐。
senses.why: Latin addere is ad- 'to' plus dare 'give': the core action is giving one thing to another, so that two things stand together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 addere 由 ad-「向」与 dare「给」构成：核心动作是把一个东西给到另一个东西上，让两者并置。

senses.title: To join numbers to get a total
senses.definition: to put two or more numbers or amounts together in order to work out their total
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多的数或量合在一起，求出它们的总数
senses.example: If you add seven and three, you get ten.
senses.exampleCN: 七加三等于十。
senses.why: Numbers are treated like objects in a pile: each is given to the pile, and the pile is then counted.
senses.whyCN: 数字被当作堆在一起的物件：每个都「给」到堆上，再数这一堆的总量。

senses.title: To say something more
senses.definition: to say something further, especially to give extra information or to make a remark after what has already been said
senses.definitionCN: 再说一些话，尤指在已说的话之后补充信息或加一句评论
senses.example: She added that the meeting would start an hour later.
senses.exampleCN: 她补充说会议将推迟一小时开始。
senses.why: Words are given to the conversation the same way sugar is given to tea: the sentence is placed on top of what was already there.
senses.whyCN: 话语被「给」到对话里，就像糖被给到茶里：新句子叠在已经说过的话之上。

senses.title: To give an extra quality
senses.definition: to bring a quality such as flavour, colour or atmosphere to something, so that it becomes richer
senses.definitionCN: 为某物带来味道、色彩或气氛等特质，使之更丰富
senses.example: A few candles added warmth to the plain room.
senses.exampleCN: 几支蜡烛给这间素净的屋子增添了暖意。
senses.why: What is given here is not a thing but a quality; the gesture of giving is unchanged, only the gift is abstract.
senses.whyCN: 这里给出去的不是物件而是一种特质；「给」的动作没有变，变的只是所给之物的抽象程度。

senses.title: To include someone in an online contact list
senses.definition: to include someone in your list of friends or contacts on a social media or messaging service
senses.definitionCN: 把某人加入社交平台或通讯软件的好友、联系人列表
senses.example: He added me on the app the day after the party.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会第二天他在那个应用上把我加为好友。
senses.why: The list is a container like the cup, and a person is the thing given to it; the old gesture simply moved online.
senses.whyCN: 好友列表就像那只杯子，人就是被放进去的东西；古老的「给」只是搬到了网上。

senses.title: To make a problem or feeling greater
senses.titleCN: 使增加；加重（麻烦、花费、情绪）
senses.definition: to increase the size, cost or unpleasantness of something that is already there, usually unintentionally
senses.definitionCN: 使已经存在的事物规模、花费或糟糕程度上升，通常是并非有意造成的
senses.example: The long delay added to everyone's frustration.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的延误让大家更加烦躁。
senses.why: Nothing new is created; one load is laid on another, and the whole pile grows heavier.
senses.whyCN: 并没有造出新东西，只是把一份负担叠到另一份上，整堆就更沉了。

senses.title: Add up: to calculate a total
senses.definition: in the phrase add up, to calculate the total of several numbers or amounts
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 add up，把若干数字或金额加起来求出总数
senses.example: Please add up these receipts before we leave.
senses.exampleCN: 我们走之前请把这些收据加起来。
senses.why: The base sense of putting things to one heap is applied to figures: the heap is then counted as a single amount.
senses.whyCN: 把东西堆到一起的基本义被用到数字上：堆好之后再当作一个总量来数。

senses.title: Add up: to seem reasonable
senses.definition: in the phrase add up, of facts or accounts, to seem reasonable and consistent when they are considered together
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 add up，指各种事实或说法放在一起看时显得合理、前后一致
senses.example: His story sounds fine, but the dates just don't add up.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法听着不错，可日期就是对不上。
senses.why: If the parts do not sum correctly, the account is wrong; the arithmetic image is used for a story that fails to hang together.
senses.whyCN: 如果各部分加起来对不上总数，这笔账就有问题；于是用算术的画面来形容一个前后拼不拢的说法。

intro.en: Add is Latin addere taken into English almost unchanged; the whole family grows from the verb dare, 'to give'.
intro.cn: add 几乎原样借自拉丁语 addere，整个词族都从动词 dare「给」生长出来。

items.en: Dare meant 'to give' and is one of the oldest recorded Latin verbs. It goes back to a reconstructed Indo-European root usually written *deh₃-, 'to give'.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，是拉丁语中有记录的最古老动词之一。它可追溯到一般写作 *deh₃- 的原始印欧语重构词根，意为「给」。

items.en: The prefix ad- 'to' plus dare formed addere, 'to give to, put to, add'. Classical Latin already used it for both objects and numbers.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 表示「向」，与 dare 合成 addere，意为「给到……上、放上去、增加」。古典拉丁语已用它表示物件与数字。

items.en: English took add straight from Latin, and it is recorded from the late fourteenth century in the general sense of putting one thing to another.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 add，自十四世纪后期有记录，泛指把一物加到另一物上。

items.en: The arithmetic sense settled early, and the phrase add up, first meaning to sum figures, appears in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 算术义很早就固定下来；短语 add up 最初表示把数字加总，见于十八世纪。

items.en: New containers brought new uses: add a friend, add to cart, add a comment. The old pattern of giving one thing to another is unchanged.
items.cn: 新的「容器」带来新用法：加好友、加入购物车、添加评论；「把一物给到另一物上」的旧结构没有变。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived nouns and one snaky false friend; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of putting something in or joining it on.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生名词，外加一个只是长得像的词；近义组收放入、附加、插入与求和一类的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adding, the thing added, or the arithmetic operation of finding a sum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加、增加物、加法」，指添加的行为、被添加之物或求和的运算。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning extra or added on top of what already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、附加的」，指在已有之物上再加的。

entries.definition: Something added at the end of a book or agreement, from the Latin gerundive of addere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补遗、附加条款」，指书或协议末尾追加的内容，来自拉丁语 addere 的动形词。

entries.definition: A small poisonous snake; it looks like add plus -er but descends from Old English nædre.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蝰蛇」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自古英语 nædre，与 add 无关。

entries.definition: To have something as a part of a group or whole, rather than putting it in from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「包括、包含」，指某物本来就是整体的一部分，而不是从外面放进去。

entries.definition: To attach something at the end of a document or list; formal and often technical.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「附加、附上」，指在文件或列表末尾添上，语气正式，多用于技术语境。

entries.definition: To put something inside something else, often into a text or a narrow space.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「插入、嵌入」，指把某物放进另一物内部，常用于文本或狭窄空间。

entries.definition: As a verb, to add amounts or figures together, or to summarize; the mathematical twin of add.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合计、总结」，指把金额或数字加在一起，是 add 在算术上的近义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb dare and the everyday patterns add appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子借助拉丁动词 dare 与 add 常见的日常结构。

normal.en: Addere is ad- plus dare, so to add is literally to give something to something.
normal.cn: addere 就是 ad- 加 dare，所以「添加」字面上就是「把一个东西给另一个」。

normal.en: Addition, additional and additionally all keep the same base.
normal.cn: addition、additional、additionally 都保留同一个词基。

normal.en: You add milk to tea, add numbers in maths, and add a word at the end of a sentence.
normal.cn: 往茶里加牛奶，在算术里加数字，在句子末尾加一句话，用的都是同一个词。

normal.en: Add up means both to total figures and, informally, to make sense.
normal.cn: add up 既指把数字加总，也口语地指「说得通」。

normal.en: Add fuel to the fire and add insult to injury both mean making a bad thing worse.
normal.cn: add fuel to the fire 与 add insult to injury 都是把坏事弄得更糟。

abstract.en: A cup already full can still take one more spoon of sugar; there is always room for one more.
abstract.cn: 杯子已经满了，却还能再放一勺糖：总还有放一样东西的余地。

abstract.en: Growing a pile and growing a number are the same gesture in two worlds.
abstract.cn: 堆高东西和累加数字，是同一个动作在两个世界里发生。

abstract.en: A story adds up only when every piece has been given its place.
abstract.cn: 一个说法要每一块都放对位置，才「加得起来」。

examples.en: Add a little milk if the sauce looks too thick.
examples.cn: 酱汁看着太稠就再加一点牛奶。

examples.en: She added my number to the group chat.
examples.cn: 她把我的号码加进了群聊。

examples.en: The numbers don't add up, so check the bill again.
examples.cn: 这些数对不上，再核对一遍账单吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德」——阿德往锅里又加一勺，味道就对了：添加、加上。

root: 拉丁语 addere 由 ad-「向」+ dare「给」构成，字面是「给到……上」，故有「添加、加上」。dare 可追溯到原始印欧语重构词根 *deh₃-「给」；addition、additional 均由这个词干加后缀构成。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses perform one act of giving something to something already there: an ingredient, a number, a remark, a quality, a contact, a burden, a column of figures, or a set of facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项做的都是同一个动作——把某样东西给到已有之物上：配料、数字、一句话、一种特质、一个联系人、一份负担、一列数字，或一组事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spoon of sugar is tipped into a cup that already holds water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺糖被倒进已经盛着水的杯子里。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER: a cup, a recipe or a contact list receives one more thing.
branches.cn: 容器线：杯子、菜谱或联系人列表再接收一样东西。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: figures are heaped and then counted as one sum.
branches.cn: 数字线：把数堆在一起，再当作一个总和来数。

branches.en: THE REMARK: one more sentence is laid on top of what has been said.
branches.cn: 言语线：在已经说过的话上再叠一句。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: what is given is warmth, colour or flavour rather than an object.
branches.cn: 特质线：给出去的是暖意、色彩或味道，而不是物件。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: a heavier pile and a story that will not sum both show the arithmetic image at work.
branches.cn: 比喻线：更沉的负担与加不拢的说法，都显出算术这一比喻在起作用。

intro.en: Add is a Latin prefix plus the verb dare, and English adds its usual noun and adjective suffixes to the stem.
intro.cn: add 由一个拉丁前缀与动词 dare 构成，英语再给这个词干加上常见的名词与形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Dare, addere, additio and addendum are all recorded Latin forms; the Indo-European root behind dare is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: dare、addere、additio 与 addendum 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；dare 背后的印欧词根属于重构形式。

senses.title: A thing that is added
senses.definition: a person or thing that is added to an existing group, collection or place and makes it larger or better
senses.definitionCN: 被加入到已有的群体、收藏或地方之中，使其更大或更好的东西或人
senses.example: The new wing is a welcome addition to the library.
senses.exampleCN: 新建的侧楼是这座图书馆很受欢迎的新增部分。
senses.why: Latin additio comes from addere, 'to give to'; the noun first names the act, then the thing that has been given to the whole.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 additio 出自 addere「给到……上」；这个名词先指「给」的动作，再指被给到整体里的那件东西。

senses.title: The act or process of adding
senses.definition: the act of putting something together with something else, so that the whole is increased
senses.definitionCN: 把某物与另一物放到一起，使整体增加的行为或过程
senses.example: The addition of a lift made the old building usable for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 加装电梯之后，这栋老楼人人都能用了。
senses.why: Before there is a new thing, there is the act of putting it in; the same noun covers both the doing and its result.
senses.whyCN: 先有「放进去」这个动作，才有新多出来的东西；同一个名词既指动作，也指结果。

senses.title: The arithmetic operation of combining numbers
senses.definition: the mathematical operation in which two or more numbers are combined to produce a sum
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多的数合成一个总和的数学运算
senses.example: Children usually learn addition before multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们通常先学加法，再学乘法。
senses.why: Arithmetic keeps the most literal image: one amount is given to another, and the result is the heap counted together.
senses.whyCN: 算术保留了最字面的画面：一笔数被给到另一笔上，结果就是把这一堆合起来数。

senses.title: An extension built onto a building
senses.definition: a new part built onto an existing house or other building
senses.definitionCN: 在原有房屋或其他建筑上加盖出来的新部分
senses.example: They built a small addition at the back of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在房子后面加盖了一个小房间。
senses.why: A building grows the same way a pile does: a new piece is given to the old structure and joined to it.
senses.whyCN: 房子长大的方式和堆东西一样：把新的一块给到旧结构上，并与它接起来。

senses.title: A new member of a family or group
senses.definition: a person, especially a baby, who has recently joined a family, or a new member of a team or group
senses.definitionCN: 新近加入家庭的人，尤指婴儿；也指团队或群体里的新成员
senses.example: The baby is the newest addition to their family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个宝宝是他们家最新添的成员。
senses.why: A person can be the thing given to a household just as a book is given to a shelf; the warmth of the phrase comes from that gift.
senses.whyCN: 人可以像一本书被放上书架那样，被「给」到一个家庭里；这个说法里的暖意正来自这份「赠予」。

senses.title: In addition: besides, as another point
senses.definition: in the phrase in addition, used to introduce one more fact, reason or item after what has already been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in addition，在已说过的内容之后再引入一个事实、理由或项目
senses.example: In addition, the museum stays open late on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，博物馆周五延长开放时间。
senses.why: The noun of adding becomes a linking phrase: one more item is given to the list of things already mentioned.
senses.whyCN: 表示「添加」的名词变成了连接短语：在已经提到的一串内容上再给一项。

senses.title: In addition to: as well as
senses.definition: in the phrase in addition to, used before a noun to mean as well as that thing, not instead of it
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in addition to，置于名词前，表示「除该物之外还」，而不是取而代之
senses.example: In addition to the fee, you pay for postage.
senses.exampleCN: 除了手续费，你还要付邮费。
senses.why: The same gesture is made explicit: one item is given on top of another, and both are kept.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作被说得更明白：把一项加在另一项之上，两项都保留。

senses.title: A chemical addition reaction
senses.definition: in chemistry, a reaction in which two molecules combine to form a single new molecule without losing any atoms
senses.definitionCN: 化学中指两个分子结合成一个新分子、不丢失任何原子的反应
senses.example: The addition of hydrogen to the double bond changes it into a single bond.
senses.exampleCN: 氢加成到双键上，双键就变成了单键。
senses.why: The technical sense is the literal one again: two whole units are joined, and nothing is taken away.
senses.whyCN: 这个专业义又回到最字面的意思：两个完整单位合在一起，什么也没有被拿走。

intro.en: Addition is a Latin noun of action built on addere, and it reached English through Old French with the arithmetic sense already attached.
intro.cn: addition 是建立在 addere 之上的拉丁语动作名词，经由古法语进入英语时，算术义已经附着其上。

items.en: Addere was ad-, 'to', plus dare, 'to give': 'to give to, put to, add'. The root behind dare is a reconstructed Indo-European form meaning 'to give'.
items.cn: addere 是 ad-「向」加 dare「给」，意为「给到……上、放上去、增加」。dare 背后的词根是表示「给」的原始印欧语重构形式。

items.en: The noun additio, 'an adding, an addition', was formed with the action-noun suffix -tio; the stem addit- is what English later took over.
items.cn: 名词 additio 意为「添加、增加」，由动作名词后缀 -tio 构成；英语后来接过的正是 addit- 这个词干。

items.en: Old French addicion carried the word toward English, and the spelling with -tion was restored later under Latin influence.
items.cn: 古法语 addicion 把这个词带向英语，后来在拉丁语影响下又恢复了 -tion 的拼写。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, with both the general sense and the arithmetic sense in use.
items.cn: 这个名词自十四世纪起在英语中有记录，一般义与算术义当时都在使用。

items.en: The linking phrases in addition and in addition to spread in the seventeenth century; the chemical sense of an addition reaction belongs to modern chemistry.
items.cn: 连接短语 in addition 与 in addition to 在十七世纪流行；「加成反应」的化学义则属于现代化学。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the add family plus edition, which shares the gift root under a different prefix; the near-meaning group gathers words for something extra.
note.cn: 形近组收 add 这一族词，外加前缀不同但同出「给」这个词根的 edition；近义组收表示额外之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed, meaning to put one thing together with another.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的动词原形，义为「添加、加上、相加」，名词即由它构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning extra, formed from addition with the suffix -al.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、附加的」，由 addition 加后缀 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A substance added in small amounts to food or fuel; formed with the suffix -ive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」，指少量加入食品或燃料中的物质；由同一词干加后缀 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: A particular version of a book or newspaper; it shares the Latin root dare but not the prefix ad-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本、版次」；与本词同出拉丁语 dare「给」，但用的是前缀 ex-，并非 ad-。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or complete a thing, often sold separately.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充物、增刊」，指为改进或补全而外加的东西，常单独出售。

entries.definition: An extra part added to a building or a period added to a deadline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「扩建部分、延长期」，指加在建筑上的部分或延长的期限。

entries.definition: An additional item that costs more or is not strictly necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「额外的东西、额外的」，口语常用，指多花钱或并非必需的部分。

entries.definition: A small amount by which something increases, especially in pay or figures.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增量、加薪额」，指某物小幅增加的数量，多用于工资或数据，语气正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Latin noun back to addere and then through the common phrases and school arithmetic.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把拉丁名词追回到 addere，再串起常见短语与学校里的算术。

normal.en: Ad- plus dare gives addere, and additio is simply that verb with an action-noun suffix.
normal.cn: ad- 加 dare 得到 addere，additio 只是给这个动词加上动作名词后缀。

normal.en: In addition and in addition to both keep the new item and never replace anything.
normal.cn: in addition 与 in addition to 都保留被加进来的东西，从不取代原有之物。

normal.en: An addition to a house is a room; an addition to a family is a baby.
normal.cn: 房子上的 addition 是一个房间，家庭里的 addition 是一个宝宝。

normal.en: Addition and subtraction are the first two operations children learn.
normal.cn: addition 与 subtraction 是孩子最先学的两种运算。

normal.en: The adjective is additional, the adverb additionally, and the food substance is an additive.
normal.cn: 形容词是 additional，副词是 additionally，食品里的添加物叫 additive。

abstract.en: A shelf does not become a new shelf; it simply holds one more row.
abstract.cn: 书架不会变成另一个书架，它只是多放了一排。

abstract.en: Adding keeps the old and brings the new; nothing is swapped out.
abstract.cn: 添加保留旧的、带来新的，没有哪一样被换掉。

abstract.en: The same word names the hand that adds and the thing that was added.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指添加的那只手，也指被加进来的那样东西。

examples.en: This chair is a useful addition to the small balcony.
examples.cn: 这把椅子给小阳台添了个实用的位置。

examples.en: In addition to the rent, we pay for water and electricity.
examples.cn: 除了房租，我们还要付水电费。

examples.en: She is studying addition and subtraction this term.
examples.cn: 她这学期在学加法和减法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪申」——阿迪往架子上再添一本书，格子就多了一格：增添物、加法。

root: 拉丁语 additio「添加、增加」由 addere「给到……上」加动作名词后缀 -tio 构成，词干 addit- 进入英语后作 addition；addere 则可拆为 ad-「向」+ dare「给」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one gesture of putting something to something that already exists: the thing, the act, the sum, an extension, a new member, the two linking phrases, and a chemical joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是同一个动作——把某物给到已有之物上：那件东西、那个动作、那个和、扩建部分、新成员、两个连接短语，以及化学上的结合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more row of books is set on a shelf that already holds rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：在已经放着几排书的架子上再放一排。

branches.en: THE THING: what has been given to the whole now stands there as a new item.
branches.cn: 物件线：被给到整体里的那样东西，如今作为新添之物立在那里。

branches.en: THE ACT: the gesture of putting it in comes before the result.
branches.cn: 动作线：先有「放进去」这个动作，才有随之而来的结果。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: numbers and molecules are joined whole, with nothing removed.
branches.cn: 运算线：数字与分子都是整块地合在一起，没有东西被拿走。

branches.en: THE GROWING WHOLE: a house gains a room, and a family gains a member.
branches.cn: 生长线：房子多出一间房，家庭多出一位成员。

branches.en: THE PHRASES: in addition and in addition to place one more item on the list already spoken.
branches.cn: 短语线：in addition 与 in addition to 在已经说出的清单上再放一项。

intro.en: Addition is a Latin verb plus an action-noun suffix, and English builds the rest of the family with -al, -ly and -ive.
intro.cn: addition 是一个拉丁动词加动作名词后缀构成的，英语再用 -al、-ly 与 -ive 扩展出其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Addere, additio and additamentum are recorded Latin forms, so only the Indo-European root of dare is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: addere、additio 与 additamentum 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，只有 dare 的印欧词根属于重构。

scene: 食堂的米饭不够，师傅又端来一锅，还添了几样小菜。There is an additional charge for the second bowl of rice.

senses.title: Extra money to be paid
senses.definition: of a charge, fee or cost, added to the basic price and paid on top of it
senses.definitionCN: 指收费、费用或成本在基本价格之外另加，需要额外支付
senses.example: There is an additional charge for the second bowl of rice.
senses.exampleCN: 第二碗米饭要另外收费。
senses.why: Additional is addition plus -al: it describes whatever has been given to the bill, so the old amount still stands and one line is added.
senses.whyCN: additional 是 addition 加 -al 构成的：它形容被加到账单上的那部分，原来的数目分毫未动，只是多了一行。

senses.title: Further information or details
senses.definition: of information or details, given in order to complete or clarify what has already been provided
senses.definitionCN: 指信息或细节是为了补全或澄清已经提供的内容而给出的
senses.example: Call this number if you need additional information.
senses.exampleCN: 需要更多信息请拨打这个号码。
senses.why: What is given here is knowledge rather than money, but it is still laid on top of what the listener already has.
senses.whyCN: 这里给出去的是知识而不是钱，但依然是叠在听者已知内容之上的补充。

senses.title: More time allowed
senses.definition: of time, allowed beyond the period that was first arranged or expected
senses.definitionCN: 指在最初安排或预计的时间之外又给出的时间
senses.example: The examiner gave us ten minutes of additional time.
senses.exampleCN: 考官多给了我们十分钟。
senses.why: Time is treated as a measured heap too: the first portion is kept, and one more portion is given to it.
senses.whyCN: 时间同样被当成一份可量的东西：原有的那份保留，再给一份叠上去。

senses.title: Extra people or seats
senses.definition: of people or places, brought in beyond the number already planned or provided
senses.definitionCN: 指人或位置在原有计划或配备之外再增添的
senses.example: The restaurant put out additional chairs for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 餐厅为婚礼多摆了一些椅子。
senses.why: The same word counts people and chairs: each new unit is added to the row without taking the place of an old one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也用来数人和椅子：每一个新单位都被加到那一排里，而不占用旧的位置。

senses.title: Extra terms in an agreement
senses.definition: of terms, conditions or rules, written into an agreement in addition to the main ones
senses.definitionCN: 指条款、条件或规则在主要条款之外又被写进协议之中
senses.example: Please read the additional terms before you sign.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前请先读一下附加条款。
senses.why: A contract is a list like any other; a new clause is given to the list and the old clauses keep their force.
senses.whyCN: 合同和别的清单一样：新条款被加进清单，旧条款的效力一条不减。

senses.title: Further evidence in a case
senses.definition: of evidence or proof, offered to strengthen what has already been presented in a case or inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 指证据或证明是为加强案件中已提交的材料而提出的
senses.example: The court allowed additional evidence from the defence.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭允许辩方提交补充证据。
senses.why: The first body of proof is left standing, and one more body is set beside it; nothing is withdrawn.
senses.whyCN: 原有的证据仍然成立，只是在旁边再摆上一份，什么也没有撤回。

senses.title: Extra help for someone who needs it
senses.definition: of help, teaching or care, provided beyond the ordinary level because someone needs more
senses.definitionCN: 指帮助、教学或照护超出常规水平，因为某人需要更多
senses.example: Pupils with additional support needs work in smaller groups.
senses.exampleCN: 需要额外支持的学生分成更小的组上课。
senses.why: The ordinary provision is not cut; another layer of help is given on top of it, which is the whole point of the word.
senses.whyCN: 常规的供给并没有减少，而是在其上再给一层帮助——这正是这个词的要害。

senses.title: An extra person covered by insurance
senses.definition: in insurance, of a driver, person or amount, included in a policy on top of the main cover
senses.definitionCN: 保险中指在主保单之外另行纳入的驾驶人、人员或金额
senses.example: The policy covers an additional driver at no extra cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单可以免费多保一名驾驶人。
senses.why: A policy is a list of covered names and sums; one more name or sum is added, and the original cover remains intact.
senses.whyCN: 保单就是一份受保名字与金额的清单：再加一个名字或一笔数目，原有的保障仍然完整。

intro.en: Additional is an English adjective made from the noun addition plus the suffix -al; the history below the noun is the history of add.
intro.cn: additional 是英语用名词 addition 加后缀 -al 构成的形容词；再往下追，就是 add 的历史。

items.en: Addere, 'to give to, put to, add', was ad-, 'to', plus dare, 'to give'. The root behind dare is a reconstructed Indo-European form.
items.cn: addere 意为「给到……上、放上去、增加」，由 ad-「向」加 dare「给」构成；dare 背后的词根是原始印欧语重构形式。

items.en: The action noun additio, 'an adding, an addition', supplied the stem addit- that passed through French into English.
items.cn: 动作名词 additio 意为「添加、增加」，提供了经法语进入英语的词干 addit-。

items.en: The noun addition is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, with both the general and the arithmetic senses.
items.cn: 名词 addition 自十四世纪起在英语中有记录，一般义与算术义并存。

items.en: The adjective additional was formed in English by adding -al to addition; the first records belong to the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 additional 是英语在 addition 后加 -al 构成的，最早记录见于十七世纪。

items.en: Its reach widened to institutions: additional support in schools, additional terms in contracts, an additional driver on a policy.
items.cn: 它的适用范围扩展到各种制度：学校的额外支持、合同的附加条款、保单上的附加驾驶人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun, adverb and verb of the same family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of extra and further.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的名词、副词与动词；近义组收表示「额外、进一步」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun from which the adjective is formed, meaning the act or thing added, or the operation of adding.
entries.definitionCN: 本词所由构成的名词，义为「添加、增加物、加法」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning besides or in addition; formed with the suffix -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此外、另外」，由本词加后缀 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A substance added to food or fuel, or an adjective meaning relating to addition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」，也可作形容词表示「添加的」，由同一词干加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: The verb at the root of the family, meaning to put one thing together with another.
entries.definitionCN: 整个词族的动词原形，义为「添加、加上、相加」。

entries.definition: More than the usual or expected amount; common in speech and often about money.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、多加的」，口语常用，常与钱有关。

entries.definition: Additional in the sense of more of the same, especially of information, action or distance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进一步的、更多的」，多指同类事物再加一层，尤用于信息、行动或距离。

entries.definition: Provided to complete or strengthen something, rather than simply to enlarge it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「补充的、辅助的」，强调补足或加强，而不只是把量变大，语气正式。

entries.definition: Kept in reserve and ready to be used if needed, as in a spare key or spare room.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「备用的」，指留作后备、需要时才用，如备用钥匙或空余房间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work through the noun addition, the adjective suffix and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子借助名词 addition、形容词后缀以及这个词常见的固定搭配来记忆。

normal.en: Additional is simply addition with the adjective suffix -al.
normal.cn: additional 就是 addition 加上形容词后缀 -al。

normal.en: At no additional cost is the phrase shops use to say the price will not go up.
normal.cn: at no additional cost 是商家说明价格不会上涨时用的固定说法。

normal.en: Additional time on an exam and additional seats in a hall are the same extra portion.
normal.cn: 考试多给的时间和大厅多摆的座位，是同一种「多出来的一份」。

normal.en: In contracts, additional terms are clauses added while the old ones stay in force.
normal.cn: 合同里的 additional terms 是新增条款，旧条款依然有效。

normal.en: The adverb additionally opens a sentence the way in addition does.
normal.cn: 副词 additionally 像 in addition 一样，用来在句首再补一层。

abstract.en: One more line under a bill: nothing above it is erased.
abstract.cn: 账单底下多出一行：上面那一行一个字也没被擦掉。

abstract.en: Extra is always measured against a first amount; without the first, there is no additional.
abstract.cn: 「额外」总要对照着先前的一份来量；没有先前那份，就谈不上额外。

abstract.en: Adding a layer makes the whole wider, not different in kind.
abstract.cn: 加一层只会让整体更宽，而不会让它变成另一种东西。

examples.en: There is an additional fee for changing the date.
examples.cn: 更改日期需要另付一笔费用。

examples.en: We need additional information before we decide.
examples.cn: 决定之前我们还需要一些补充信息。

examples.en: The airline offered additional time to rebook.
examples.cn: 航空公司多给了改签的时间。

root: 由名词 addition 加形容词后缀 -al 构成；addition 出自拉丁语 additio「添加」，再往下是 addere「给到……上」，即 ad-「向」+ dare「给」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses describe one more portion laid on an existing whole: money, information, time, people, contract terms, evidence, help, or insurance cover.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项说的都是叠在已有整体上的一份：钱、信息、时间、人、合同条款、证据、帮助，或保险保障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one new line is written under an existing bill, and everything above it stays.
core.cn: 核心意象：在已有账单下面添一行，上面的一切照旧。

branches.en: THE BILL: the basic price stands and one more sum is charged.
branches.cn: 账单线：基本价格不动，另收一笔。

branches.en: THE RECORD: details and evidence are supplied to complete what is already on file.
branches.cn: 记录线：补充信息与证据，为的是补全已经备案的材料。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the period already agreed is kept, and more is granted.
branches.cn: 时间线：原先约定的时长保留，再多给一段。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: chairs, staff and help are added for those who need more.
branches.cn: 人的线：为需要更多的人加椅子、加人手、加帮助。

branches.en: THE PAPER: clauses and policies gain one more item without losing any old one.
branches.cn: 文书线：合同与保单多一项，旧的保障一项不少。
